items.title: The selective Lueders update by an orthogonal projection
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $P$ be an orthogonal projection on $H$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]) and let $\rho$ be a density operator with $p:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P)>0$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)). Define the **selective update**
$$\rho_{P}:=\frac{P\rho P}{p}.$$
Then:

(a) $P\rho P$ is a positive trace-class operator with $\operatorname{tr}(P\rho P)=p$, so $\rho_{P}$ is a density operator;

(b) $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{P}P)=1$ and
$$P\rho_{P}P=\rho_{P}=P\rho_{P}=\rho_{P}P;$$
in particular $\rho_{P}$ commutes with $P$ and is fixed by compression with $P$;

(c) if $Q$ is an orthogonal projection with $QP=0$, then $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{P}Q)=0$ and $Q\rho_{P}Q=0$;

(d) if $\rho=T_{u,u}$ for a unit vector $u$ with $Pu\ne0$, where $T_{u,u}x=\langle x,u\rangle u$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]), then $\rho_{P}=T_{Pu,Pu}/\|Pu\|^{2}$, the pure state of the normalized vector $Pu$; the value depends only on the ray of $Pu$.

No physical interpretation of the update is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A nonzero complex Hilbert space $H$; an orthogonal projection $P$ on $H$; a density operator $\rho$ with $p=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P)>0$; an orthogonal projection $Q$ with $QP=0$; a unit vector $u$ with $Pu\ne0$.

[F1] **Orthogonal projections.** An orthogonal projection $P$ on $H$ is a bounded linear operator with $P^{2}=P=P^{*}$, $\|P\|\le1$ and $\langle Px,y\rangle=\langle x,Py\rangle$ for all $x,y\in H$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]).

[F2] **Density operators.** A density operator $\rho$ is self-adjoint, positive and trace class with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$, and it admits an expansion $\rho=\sum_{n}w_{n}T_{u_{n},u_{n}}$ with $(u_{n})$ a finite or countable orthonormal family and weights $w_{n}\ge0$, $\sum_{n}w_{n}=1$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)).

[F3] **Rank-one calculus.** $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ is trace class with $\operatorname{tr}(T_{u,v})=\langle u,v\rangle$ and $\|T_{u,v}\|_{1}=\|u\|\,\|v\|$; $T_{x,x}\ge0$ with $\operatorname{tr}(T_{x,x})=\|x\|^{2}$; and for bounded $B$ one has $BT_{u,v}=T_{Bu,v}$ and $T_{u,v}B=T_{u,B^{*}v}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] clauses (b), (c) and (d)).

[F4] **Trace-class ideal and cyclicity.** If $T$ is trace class and $B$ bounded, then $BT$ and $TB$ are trace class with $\operatorname{tr}(BT)=\operatorname{tr}(TB)$ and $\operatorname{tr}$ linear and trace-norm continuous ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-nuclear-bounded-cyclicity]] clause (b)).

[F5] **Positivity of quadratic forms.** If $S\ge0$ then $\langle Sx,x\rangle\ge0$ for every $x$; sums of positive operators are positive, and $\rho=T_{u,u}$ with $\|u\|=1$ is a density operator ([[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]], [F2], [F3]).

## Proof

1.1 [The unnormalized update] Since $P=P^{*}$ and $\rho=\rho^{*}$ by [F1] and [F2], $(P\rho P)^{*}=P^{*}\rho^{*}P^{*}=P\rho P$, so $P\rho P$ is self-adjoint. For $x\in H$, $\langle P\rho Px,x\rangle=\langle\rho Px,Px\rangle\ge0$ by [F1] and [F5], so $P\rho P\ge0$. With $P$ bounded and $\rho$ trace class, $\rho P$ and then $P(\rho P)=P\rho P$ are trace class by [F4], and $\operatorname{tr}(P\rho P)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho PP)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P)=p$ by cyclicity [F4] and $P^{2}=P$ [F1]. [given, F1, F2, F4, F5, algebra]

2.1 [Clause (a)] Since $p>0$, the operator $\rho_{P}=P\rho P/p$ is self-adjoint and positive with trace $p/p=1$, hence a density operator by [F2]; this is (a). [step 1.1, F2, algebra]

2.2 [Clause (b)] By $P^{2}=P$ and cyclicity [F4], $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{P}P)=\operatorname{tr}(P\rho PP)/p=\operatorname{tr}(\rho PPP)/p=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P)/p=1$. Moreover $P\rho_{P}P=P(P\rho P)P/p=P\rho P/p=\rho_{P}$ and $P\rho_{P}=PP\rho P/p=\rho_{P}=\rho_{P}PP=\rho_{P}P$; thus $\rho_{P}$ commutes with $P$ and is fixed by compression with $P$. This is (b). [step 1.1, F1, F4, algebra]

2.3 [Clause (c)] If $QP=0$ then $Q\rho_{P}Q=QP\rho PQ/p=0$ as an operator identity, and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{P}Q)=\operatorname{tr}(P\rho PQ)/p=\operatorname{tr}(QP\rho P)/p=0$ by cyclicity [F4]. This is (c). [step 1.1, F4, algebra]

3.1 [Clause (d)] Let $\rho=T_{u,u}$ with $\|u\|=1$. By [F3], $P\rho P=PT_{u,u}P=T_{Pu,u}P=T_{Pu,Pu}$, whose trace is $\|Pu\|^{2}>0$, and $p=\operatorname{tr}(T_{u,u}P)=\operatorname{tr}(PT_{u,u})=\langle Pu,u\rangle=\|Pu\|^{2}$ by [F3] and cyclicity [F4]; hence $\rho_{P}=T_{Pu,Pu}/\|Pu\|^{2}$. For $z\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$ the identity $T_{zPu,zPu}=|z|^{2}T_{Pu,Pu}$ from the conjugate-linearity of $(u,v)\mapsto T_{u,v}$ [F3] shows that the state depends only on the ray of $Pu$. This is (d). [step 1.1, F3, F4, algebra] ∎

items.title: The non-selective Lueders map and the discarded-outcome ensemble
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ be a finite or countably infinite family of pairwise orthogonal orthogonal projections on $H$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]) whose strong sum is the identity,
$$\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}x=x\qquad(x\in H),$$
let $\rho$ be a density operator ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)), and put $p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})$. Define the **non-selective Lueders map**
$$\Phi(\rho):=\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}\rho P_{a}.$$
Then:

(a) the series converges in trace norm; $\Phi(\rho)$ is a positive trace-class operator with $\operatorname{tr}\Phi(\rho)=1$, hence a density operator, and $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a}P_{a}\Phi(\rho)P_{a}$;

(b) for every $b$, $P_{b}\Phi(\rho)=\Phi(\rho)P_{b}=P_{b}\Phi(\rho)P_{b}=P_{b}\rho P_{b}$; in particular $\Phi(\rho)$ commutes with every $P_{b}$;

(c) *discarded-outcome ensemble.* $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\rho_{a}$, where $\rho_{a}=P_{a}\rho P_{a}/p_{a}$ is the selective update of [[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]]; the series converges in trace norm;

(d) if $B\in\mathcal B(H)$ is bounded and $P_{a}B=BP_{a}$ for every $a$, then $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho B)$;

(e) if $\psi=\alpha u+\beta v$ with $u,v$ orthonormal, $u\in\operatorname{ran}P_{1}$, $v\in\operatorname{ran}P_{2}$ for distinct labels $1\ne2$, and $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$, then $\Phi(\rho)=|\alpha|^{2}T_{u,u}+|\beta|^{2}T_{v,v}$, and
$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\Phi(\rho)(T_{u,v}+T_{v,u})\bigr)=0,\qquad \operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(T_{u,v}+T_{v,u})\bigr)=2\operatorname{Re}(\alpha\overline{\beta});$$

(f) if $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ for a nonzero $\psi$ then $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a:P_{a}\psi\ne0}\|P_{a}\psi\|^{2}\,T_{\nu(P_{a}\psi),\nu(P_{a}\psi)}$ with $\nu$ the normalization map, the series converging in trace norm.

No physical interpretation of the map is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A nonzero complex Hilbert space $H$; pairwise orthogonal projections $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ with strong sum $I$; a density operator $\rho$; probabilities $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})$; a bounded operator $B$ commuting with every $P_{a}$; a vector $\psi=\alpha u+\beta v$.

[F1] **Countable Kraus normalization.** If $(M_{a})$ is a finite or countable family of bounded operators with $\sum_{a}M_{a}^{*}M_{a}\to I$ strongly, then $\sum_{a}\|M_{a}x\|^{2}=\|x\|^{2}$ for every $x$; for every positive trace-class $\rho$ the series $\sum_{a}M_{a}\rho M_{a}^{*}$ converges in trace norm to a positive trace-class operator with trace $\operatorname{tr}\rho$; the map extends uniquely to a trace-preserving linear positive map of the trace-class operators, and it maps density operators to density operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]] clauses (a)-(c)).

[F2] **Orthogonal projections and orthogonality.** Each $P_{a}$ satisfies $P_{a}^{2}=P_{a}=P_{a}^{*}$ and $P_{a}P_{b}=0$ for $a\ne b$; $\|P_{a}\|\le1$; the hypothesis of the Statement is that the finite partial sums $\sum_{a\le N}P_{a}$ converge strongly to $I$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]).

[F3] **Zero-probability summands vanish.** If $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})=0$, then $P_{a}\rho P_{a}=0$. Indeed, using the expansion [F3'] and trace-norm continuity of left and right multiplication by $P_{a}$, $P_{a}\rho P_{a}=\sum_{n}w_{n}T_{P_{a}u_{n},P_{a}u_{n}}$ with trace $\sum_{n}w_{n}\|P_{a}u_{n}\|^{2}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})=0$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] clauses (b) and (d)); every summand is nonnegative, so each summand vanishes and the series is $0$.

[F3'] **Expansion of a density operator.** $\rho=\sum_{n}w_{n}T_{u_{n},u_{n}}$ with $(u_{n})$ a finite or countable orthonormal family and $w_{n}\ge0$, $\sum_{n}w_{n}=1$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)).

[F4] **Rank-one calculus.** $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ is trace class with $\operatorname{tr}(T_{u,v})=\langle u,v\rangle$; $T_{x,x}\ge0$ with $\operatorname{tr}(T_{x,x})=\|x\|^{2}$; for bounded $B$, $BT_{u,v}=T_{Bu,v}$ and $T_{u,v}B=T_{u,B^{*}v}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] clauses (b)-(d)).

[F5] **Trace-class ideal and cyclicity.** For bounded $B$ and trace-class $T$, $BT$ and $TB$ are trace class with $\operatorname{tr}(BT)=\operatorname{tr}(TB)$ ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-nuclear-bounded-cyclicity]] clause (b)).

[F6] **Selective update.** For a single projection $P$ with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho P)>0$ the operator $\rho_{P}=P\rho P/\operatorname{tr}(\rho P)$ is a density operator with $P\rho_{P}P=\rho_{P}$ and $Q\rho_{P}Q=0$ for every projection $Q$ with $QP=0$ ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]] clauses (a)-(c)).

## Proof

1.1 [The map is the projection Kraus map] For each $a$, $P_{a}^{*}P_{a}=P_{a}^{2}=P_{a}$ by [F2], so $\sum_{a\le N}P_{a}^{*}P_{a}=\sum_{a\le N}P_{a}\to I$ strongly: the hypothesis of [F1] holds with $M_{a}=P_{a}$. Therefore $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a}P_{a}\rho P_{a}$ converges in trace norm, is positive trace class with $\operatorname{tr}\Phi(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$, and is a density operator. This proves the first part of (a). [given, F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 [The compressed identity] Fix $b$. Left and right multiplication by the bounded operator $P_{b}$ are continuous in trace norm, since $\|P_{b}T\|_{1}\le\|P_{b}\|\,\|T\|_{1}$ and $\|TP_{b}\|_{1}\le\|P_{b}\|\,\|T\|_{1}$ for trace-class $T$ ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]]); applying this to the trace-norm convergent series of step 1.1 gives $P_{b}\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a}P_{b}P_{a}\rho P_{a}$ and $\Phi(\rho)P_{b}=\sum_{a}P_{a}\rho P_{a}P_{b}$. Since $P_{b}P_{a}=0$ for $a\ne b$ and $P_{b}^{2}=P_{b}$ [F2], all summands vanish except $a=b$, and that summand is $P_{b}\rho P_{b}$; hence $P_{b}\Phi(\rho)=P_{b}\rho P_{b}=\Phi(\rho)P_{b}$ and therefore $P_{b}\Phi(\rho)P_{b}=P_{b}\rho P_{b}$. Summing the identity $P_{b}\Phi(\rho)P_{b}=P_{b}\rho P_{b}$ over $b$ and using step 1.1 once more gives $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{b}P_{b}\Phi(\rho)P_{b}$. This proves (a) and (b). [step 1.1, F1, F2, F5, algebra]

2.2 [The discarded-outcome mixture] For a label $a$ with $p_{a}>0$, [F6] gives $P_{a}\rho P_{a}=p_{a}\rho_{a}$ with $\rho_{a}$ a density operator, and [F3] gives $P_{a}\rho P_{a}=0$ for a label with $p_{a}=0$. Hence the summands with $p_{a}=0$ vanish and, reindexing the trace-norm convergent series of step 1.1 over the subfamily $\{a:p_{a}>0\}$, $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\rho_{a}$. This is (c). [step 1.1, F3, F6, algebra]

2.3 [Invariance under compatible bounded quantities] Let $B$ be bounded with $P_{a}B=BP_{a}$ for every $a$. Then $P_{a}B\rho P_{a}=BP_{a}\rho P_{a}$ and, using the trace-norm continuity of left multiplication by $B$ together with step 1.1, $B\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a}P_{a}(B\rho)P_{a}$. The right-hand side is the Kraus map of [F1] evaluated at the trace-class operator $B\rho$, so $\operatorname{tr}(B\Phi(\rho))=\operatorname{tr}\Phi(B\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(B\rho)$ by trace preservation; since $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)B)=\operatorname{tr}(B\Phi(\rho))$ [F5], this gives $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho B)$. This is (d). [step 1.1, F1, F5, algebra]

3.1 [Coherence destruction] Let $\psi=\alpha u+\beta v$ with $u,v$ orthonormal, $u\in\operatorname{ran}P_{1}$ and $v\in\operatorname{ran}P_{2}$, $1\ne2$, and $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$. For $a\notin\{1,2\}$ one has $P_{a}u=P_{a}P_{1}u=0$ and $P_{a}v=P_{a}P_{2}v=0$ by [F2], so $P_{a}\psi=0$; and $P_{1}\psi=\alpha u$, $P_{2}\psi=\beta v$. Hence the series has only two nonzero summands, and [F4] gives $P_{1}\rho P_{1}=T_{P_{1}\psi,P_{1}\psi}=|\alpha|^{2}T_{u,u}$ and $P_{2}\rho P_{2}=|\beta|^{2}T_{v,v}$, so $\Phi(\rho)=|\alpha|^{2}T_{u,u}+|\beta|^{2}T_{v,v}$. For the pairing with $T_{u,v}$: $\operatorname{tr}(T_{u,u}T_{u,v})=\langle T_{u,u}u,v\rangle=\langle u,v\rangle=0$ and $\operatorname{tr}(T_{v,v}T_{u,v})=\langle T_{v,v}u,v\rangle=\langle u,v\rangle\langle v,v\rangle=0$, and conjugating gives the same vanishing for $T_{v,u}$; hence $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)(T_{u,v}+T_{v,u}))=0$. For the coherent state, $\operatorname{tr}(\rho T_{u,v})=\langle T_{\psi,\psi}u,v\rangle=\langle u,\psi\rangle\langle\psi,v\rangle=\overline{\alpha}\beta$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho T_{v,u})=\overline{\langle u,\psi\rangle\langle\psi,v\rangle}=\alpha\overline{\beta}$, so the cross term is $2\operatorname{Re}(\alpha\overline{\beta})$. This is (e). [step 2.2, F2, F4, algebra]

4.1 [The pure-state formula] Let $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ with $\psi\ne0$. By step 1.1 with $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ and the rank-one rules [F4], $P_{a}\rho P_{a}=T_{P_{a}\psi,P_{a}\psi}$, and $T_{P_{a}\psi,P_{a}\psi}=\|P_{a}\psi\|^{2}T_{\nu(P_{a}\psi),\nu(P_{a}\psi)}$ when $P_{a}\psi\ne0$, while both sides vanish when $P_{a}\psi=0$; the trace-norm convergence of the resulting series is that of step 1.1. This is (f). [step 1.1, F4, algebra] ∎

items.title: Declared ideal measurements and instruments of the framework
items.statement:
Adopt the state postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]] (P3) for the declared system, whose state space is $D(H)$ for the assigned nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]). Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis of the cited mathematics. The following vocabulary is used by this page.

**(a) Declared ideal sharp measurement.** A **declared ideal sharp measurement** of the system is a finite or countably infinite family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ of bounded orthogonal projections on $H$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]) that are **mutually orthogonal**, $P_{a}P_{b}=0$ for $a\ne b$, and whose **strong sum** is the identity,
$$\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}x=x\qquad(x\in H).$$
The index $a$ is the **outcome label** and the family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ is the **outcome structure** of the declared measurement; it is part of the declared apparatus model, not a quantity computed from the state. This is clause (i) of P3.

**(b) The Lueders instrument of a declared ideal sharp measurement.** For a preparation $\rho$ the **outcome probabilities** are
$$p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})\ge0,\qquad \sum_{a}p_{a}=1,$$
and for a pure preparation of the unit ray $[\psi]$ they are $p_{a}=\|P_{a}\psi\|^{2}$ (clause (ii) of P3, read with the outcome law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). If $p_{a}>0$ the **conditional state** after the outcome $a$ is the selective Lueders update
$$\rho_{a}:=\frac{P_{a}\rho P_{a}}{p_{a}};$$
it is a state with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}P_{a})=1$ and $P_{a}\rho_{a}P_{a}=\rho_{a}$ ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], clause (iii) of P3). If the outcomes are recorded but not selected, the **discarded-outcome state** is
$$\Phi(\rho):=\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}\rho P_{a},$$
the trace-norm convergent series of [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]]; it is a state with $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\rho_{a}$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)P_{a})=p_{a}$ (clause (iv) of P3).

**(c) Declared ideal filter.** A **declared ideal filter** is a declared ideal sharp measurement with exactly two outcomes $a=1,2$: the filter **passes** the component in the range of $P_{1}$ and **blocks** the component in the range of $P_{2}=I-P_{1}$. Repeated use of the filter in series means the sequential application of the conditional updates of clause (b).

**(d) Declared instrument.** A **declared finite or countable instrument** for an outcome set $A$ consists of a finite or countable family $(M_{a,r})_{\substack{a\in A\\r\in R_{a}}}$ of bounded operators on $H$ with
$$\sum_{a\in A}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}=I$$
in the strong sense ([[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]]), the **effects**
$$F_{a}:=\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r},$$
the outcome probabilities $p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$ of clause (iv) of P2, the **conditional updates**
$$\rho\longmapsto\frac{1}{p_{a}}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}\qquad(p_{a}>0),$$
and the **discarded-outcome map** $\rho\mapsto\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}$. The family $(M_{a,r})$, called the **Kraus family** of the instrument, is part of the declared apparatus model. The effects $(F_{a})$ alone do not determine the conditional updates: distinct normalized Kraus families can share the same effects while defining different updates ([[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]] clause (d); clause (v) of P3). More generally one may declare an abstract instrument $J:\Sigma\to\mathcal B(\mathcal S_{1}(H))$ in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]], of which the Kraus case is a concrete instance.

**(e) Declaration discipline.** A model of an apparatus that is used to predict post-measurement states must declare both an outcome structure (effects) and an update rule; the outcome law of P2 alone does not supply the update, and the update is not a mathematical consequence of the effects. The special case in which the Kraus family consists of the projections $P_{a}$ themselves (with a single $r$ per outcome) is the Lueders instrument of clauses (a)-(b). The claim that a concrete laboratory device realizes a particular declared measurement, filter or instrument is a physical identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), not a consequence of this definition.

**(f) Limits.** Declared ideal sharp measurements are idealizations of apparatus that are idealized as repeatable and projection-valued; the framework does not assert that every apparatus, or any particular apparatus, is of this form (clause (v) of P3). The following are outside the declared class and require their own models: a measurement of an exact value of a quantity whose spectrum is continuous (no normalization of a delta symbol is intended; clauses (iii) of P2 and (v) of P3); a photon-absorption or other destructive detector, whose declared instrument need not leave an outgoing state of the same form (clause (v) of P3); and a unitary system-apparatus interaction, which by itself produces conditional correlations without selecting a unique recorded outcome or a preferred outcome family (clause (v) of P3).

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) read P1, P2 and P3 in the measurement vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology of the page's later items; they add no assumption to those postulates. The cited mathematical items ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]]) are conditional mathematics about the displayed formulas; no physical process, outcome uniqueness or empirical fact is deduced here.

items.physical_scope: The measurement vocabulary of the non-relativistic quantum framework for declared ideal apparatus: declared ideal sharp measurements as finite or countable families of mutually orthogonal projections resolving the identity, their Lueders instrument with outcome law, conditional update and discarded-outcome map, declared ideal filters, and declared finite or countable instruments whose Kraus family or abstract instrument supplies both the outcome effects and the state update. The definition reads the adopted postulates P1, P2 and P3; it asserts no apparatus realization, no uniqueness of recorded outcomes, no collapse of exact continuum values, and no empirical result.

items.title: Consequences of a declared ideal sharp measurement: repeatability and discarded ensembles
items.statement:
Adopt the state postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2 and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate P3 of the framework ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]]), and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, the hypothesis of the cited mathematics. Let $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ be a declared ideal sharp measurement of a system with state space $D(H)$ ([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]) and let $\rho$ be a state. Then:

**(a) Outcome law.** For every outcome label $a$ the probability is $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})$, with $p_{a}\ge0$ and $\sum_{a}p_{a}=1$; for the pure state of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $p_{a}=\|P_{a}\psi\|^{2}$.

**(b) Conditional state and repeatability.** If $p_{a}>0$, the conditional state after the outcome $a$ is the state $\rho_{a}=P_{a}\rho P_{a}/p_{a}$, with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}P_{a})=1$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}P_{b})=0$ for $b\ne a$. Immediate repetition of the same declared measurement therefore returns the same outcome with certainty:
$$\mathbb P(\text{second outcome }b\mid\text{first outcome }a)=\delta_{ab}.$$

**(c) Discarded outcomes.** The discarded-outcome state $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a}P_{a}\rho P_{a}$ is a state and coincides with the outcome-weighted mixture of the conditional states,
$$\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\rho_{a},$$
the series converging in trace norm; moreover $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)P_{a})=p_{a}$ for every $a$ and $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a}P_{a}\Phi(\rho)P_{a}$. The conditional-vs-discarded distinction is therefore exactly the distinction between one selected branch $\rho_{a}$ and the mixture of all branches.

**(d) Compatible bounded quantities.** If $B$ is a bounded operator with $P_{a}B=BP_{a}$ for every $a$, then $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho B)$. In particular, if the declared measurement is the spectral measurement of a bounded assigned sharp observable $A=\sum_{a}a_{a}P_{a}$ (a finite or norm-convergent series with real $a_{a}$), then $A$ commutes with every $P_{a}$ and the mean of $A$ is unchanged by discarding the outcomes.

**(e) Loss of coherence.** If $\psi=\alpha u+\beta v$ with $u,v$ orthonormal, $u\in\operatorname{ran}P_{1}$, $v\in\operatorname{ran}P_{2}$ for distinct labels $1\ne2$, and $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$, then
$$\Phi(\rho)=|\alpha|^{2}T_{u,u}+|\beta|^{2}T_{v,v},\qquad \operatorname{tr}\bigl(\Phi(\rho)(T_{u,v}+T_{v,u})\bigr)=0,$$
whereas for the coherent preparation $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(T_{u,v}+T_{v,u}))=2\operatorname{Re}(\alpha\overline{\beta})$: the discarded-outcome ensemble is the classical mixture of the branch states and carries no coherence between the ranges of $P_{1}$ and $P_{2}$.

**(f) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) are conditional on the adopted P3 and on the mathematical items cited; they do not assert that any laboratory apparatus realizes a declared ideal sharp measurement, do not select a unique recorded outcome, and do not describe the disturbance produced by an apparatus outside the declared class (clause (v) of P3). The identification of a device with a declared measurement is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The adopted postulates P1, P2, P3; a declared ideal sharp measurement $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ with strong sum $I$; a state $\rho$; probabilities $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})$; the discarded-outcome state $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a}P_{a}\rho P_{a}$; a bounded operator $B$ commuting with every $P_{a}$; vectors $\psi,u,v$ and scalars $\alpha,\beta$ as in clause (e).

[F1] **Declared measurements.** The family $(P_{a})$ is a finite or countable family of pairwise orthogonal orthogonal projections with strong sum $I$, and its Lueders instrument has outcome probabilities $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})$, conditional states $\rho_{a}=P_{a}\rho P_{a}/p_{a}$ for $p_{a}>0$, and discarded-outcome state $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a}P_{a}\rho P_{a}$ ([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]] clauses (a)-(b); [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]] clauses (i)-(iv)).

[F2] **Selective update.** For $p_{a}>0$ the operator $\rho_{a}$ is a state with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}P_{a})=1$, $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}Q)=0$ for every orthogonal projection $Q$ with $QP_{a}=0$, and $P_{a}\rho_{a}P_{a}=\rho_{a}$ ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]] clauses (a)-(c)).

[F3] **Non-selective map.** The series $\Phi(\rho)$ converges in trace norm; $\Phi(\rho)$ is a state; $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\rho_{a}$; $P_{b}\Phi(\rho)P_{b}=P_{b}\rho P_{b}$ for every $b$, so in particular $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)P_{b})=p_{b}$; $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{b}P_{b}\Phi(\rho)P_{b}$; and for bounded $B$ commuting with every $P_{a}$ one has $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho B)$ ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]] clauses (a)-(d)).

[F4] **Rank-one pairing.** $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ is trace class with $\operatorname{tr}(T_{u,v})=\langle u,v\rangle$, and $\operatorname{tr}(S T_{u,v})=\langle Su,v\rangle$ for trace-class $S$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] clause (b), [[lem-nrqm-composites-nuclear-bounded-cyclicity]] clause (b)).

[F5] **States and mixtures.** A convex combination of states is a state; the trace is linear and trace-norm continuous ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)).

## Proof

1.1 [Clause (a)] By [F1] the outcome probabilities of the declared measurement are $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})$. Since $0\le P_{a}\le I$ and $\rho\ge0$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$, positivity of $P_{a}\rho P_{a}$ and cyclicity give $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(P_{a}\rho P_{a})\ge0$ [F2, F4]. Trace-norm convergence of $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a}P_{a}\rho P_{a}$ and continuity of the trace give $\sum_{a}p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}\Phi(\rho)=1$ by [F3]. For a pure preparation, [F1] with the rank-one calculus [F4] gives $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(T_{\psi,\psi}P_{a})=\langle P_{a}\psi,\psi\rangle=\|P_{a}\psi\|^{2}$. This is (a). [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

1.2 [Clause (e)] Under the hypotheses of clause (e), the computation of [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]] clause (e) applies verbatim to $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$: it gives $\Phi(\rho)=|\alpha|^{2}T_{u,u}+|\beta|^{2}T_{v,v}$, $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)(T_{u,v}+T_{v,u}))=0$, and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(T_{u,v}+T_{v,u}))=2\operatorname{Re}(\alpha\overline{\beta})$. This is (e). [given, F3, F4, algebra]

2.1 [Clause (b)] If $p_{a}>0$, [F2] gives that $\rho_{a}$ is a state with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}P_{a})=1$; for $b\ne a$ the projections $P_{b}$ and $P_{a}$ satisfy $P_{b}P_{a}=0$, so [F2] gives $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}P_{b})=0$. Applying the outcome law of clause (a) to the preparation $\rho_{a}$, the probability of the outcome $b$ in an immediate repetition of the same declared measurement is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}P_{b})=\delta_{ab}$. This is (b). [step 1.1, given, F1, F2, algebra]

3.1 [Clause (c)] By [F3], $\Phi(\rho)$ is a state and equals the trace-norm convergent series $\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\rho_{a}$; since $\operatorname{tr}((p_{a}\rho_{a})P_{b})=\delta_{ab}p_{a}$ by clause (b) and trace-norm continuity of the trace, summing gives $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)P_{b})=p_{b}$ for every $b$, and [F3] also gives $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{b}P_{b}\Phi(\rho)P_{b}$. This is (c). [step 2.1, given, F3, F5, algebra]

4.1 [Clause (d)] If $B$ is bounded and $P_{a}B=BP_{a}$ for every $a$, [F3] gives $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho B)$. If $A=\sum_{a}a_{a}P_{a}$ is a bounded assigned sharp observable with real coefficients $a_{a}$, then $AP_{b}=\sum_{a}a_{a}P_{a}P_{b}=a_{b}P_{b}=P_{b}A$, so $A$ commutes with every $P_{a}$ and the identity applies to $B=A$: the mean $\operatorname{tr}(\rho A)$ of the bounded observable $A$ is unchanged by discarding the outcomes. This is (d). [step 3.1, given, F3, algebra]

5.1 [Clause (f) and scope] Clauses (a)-(e) were obtained from the adopted clauses of P3 [F1] and the cited mathematical lemmas [F2, F3, F4]; no clause used a claim about a laboratory apparatus, an apparatus dynamics, or a preferred recorded outcome. Clause (v) of P3 explicitly excludes outcome uniqueness and arbitrary apparatuses from the declared class, and P7 makes the identification of a device with the declared measurement a tested identification with uncertainty. This is (f). [step 1.2, given, F1, F3, algebra] ∎

D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Section 3.3, printed pages 76-77 (Born rule, collapse and repeat measurement)

items.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the adopted ideal conditional-measurement postulate P3 for a declared ideal sharp measurement: the Born outcome probabilities, the selective Lueders conditional states, the certainty of an immediately repeated outcome, the discarded-outcome state as the outcome-weighted mixture of the conditional states, invariance of bounded quantities compatible with the declared measurement under discarding, and the loss of coherence between non-selected branches. The theorem asserts nothing about any laboratory apparatus, about outcome uniqueness or about measurements outside the declared class.

items.title: The Lueders update on a degenerate eigenspace preserves intra-eigenspace coherence
items.statement:
Adopt the state postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2 and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate P3 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]]), and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice, the hypotheses of the cited spectral mathematics. Let $A$ be a bounded assigned sharp observable of a system with state space $D(H)$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]), with spectral projection-valued measure $E_{A}$ ([[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]]), and let $\lambda$ be an eigenvalue of $A$ with eigenspace $K=\ker(A-\lambda I)$ and $P:=E_{A}(\{\lambda\})$, the orthogonal projection of $H$ onto $K$. Declare the two-outcome ideal sharp measurement $(P,I-P)$, the **$\lambda$-readout** of $A$. Let $\psi\in K$ with $\|\psi\|=1$ and let $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ be the pure state of $\psi$. Then:

**(a) Certainty and trivial update.** $p_{\lambda}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P)=1$, and the conditional state after the outcome $\lambda$ is $\rho_{\lambda}=\rho$: the $\lambda$-readout leaves this preparation unchanged.

**(b) No disturbance inside the eigenspace.** For every assigned sharp observable $C$ and every Borel set $S\subseteq\mathbb R$, the outcome law of $C$ computed in the conditional state equals its law computed in $\rho$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b)); in particular the $\lambda$-readout induces no decoherence or disturbance within the eigenspace.

**(c) Degenerate case: coherence is retained.** If $\dim K\ge2$ and $\psi=\alpha u+\beta v$ with $u,v$ orthonormal vectors of $K$ and $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$, then the conditional state is the coherent superposition $T_{\psi,\psi}$, not the mixture $|\alpha|^{2}T_{u,u}+|\beta|^{2}T_{v,v}$: for the bounded assigned sharp observable
$$W:=T_{w,w}-T_{w',w'},\qquad w:=\frac{u+v}{\sqrt2},\qquad w'=\frac{u-v}{\sqrt2},$$
the conditional state assigns probability $1$ to the value $+1$ of $W$ whenever $\alpha=\beta=1/\sqrt2$, i.e. whenever $\psi=w$, while the mixture $|\alpha|^{2}T_{u,u}+|\beta|^{2}T_{v,v}$ assigns probability $1/2$ to each of the values $+1$ and $-1$ of $W$.

**(d) Scope.** The update used here is the Lueders update with the eigenspace projection $P$ itself, as adopted in P3; no physical apparatus is asserted to perform the $\lambda$-readout without disturbance, and a declared apparatus that resolves the eigenspace further (a finer family of projections inside $K$) is a different declared measurement, not the coarse $\lambda$-readout.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The adopted postulates P1, P2, P3; a bounded assigned sharp observable $A$ with spectral PVM $E_{A}$; an eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $A$, its eigenspace $K$, and $P=E_{A}(\{\lambda\})$; a unit vector $\psi\in K$; the pure state $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$; unit vectors $u,v\in K$ with $\psi=\alpha u+\beta v$; the observables $W$, $w$, $w'$ of clause (c).

[F1] **Spectral atoms.** The projection $E_{A}(\{\lambda\})$ is the orthogonal projection of $H$ onto the eigenspace $\ker(A-\lambda I)$, and it is nonzero exactly when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$ ([[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clause (a)).

[F2] **Lueders update and outcome law.** For a declared ideal sharp measurement $(P_{a})$ the outcome probabilities are $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})$, the conditional state is $\rho_{a}=P_{a}\rho P_{a}/p_{a}$ when $p_{a}>0$, and the law of a general assigned sharp observable $C$ in a preparation $\sigma$ is $\mu^{C}_{\sigma}(S)=\operatorname{tr}(\sigma E_{C}(S))$, equal to $\|E_{C}(S)\xi\|^{2}$ for $\sigma=T_{\xi,\xi}$ ([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]] clauses (a)-(b), [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b), [[pthm-nrqm-measurement-projective-outcomes-and-discarded-ensembles]] clauses (a)-(b)).

[F3] **Selective update by a projection.** For a density operator $\sigma$, an orthogonal projection $Q$ with $\operatorname{tr}(\sigma Q)>0$, and $\xi$ a unit vector with $Q\xi=\xi$, the update of $T_{\xi,\xi}$ by $Q$ is $T_{\xi,\xi}$ ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]] clause (d), applied with $Q\xi=\xi$).

[F4] **Rank-one calculus and spectral projections.** $T_{x,y}$ is trace class with $\operatorname{tr}(T_{x,y})=\langle x,y\rangle$ and $\operatorname{tr}(ST_{x,y})=\langle Sx,y\rangle$ for trace-class $S$; for orthonormal $w,w'$ the operators $T_{w,w}$ and $T_{w',w'}$ are the orthogonal projections onto $\mathbb Cw$ and $\mathbb Cw'$, with $T_{w,w}T_{w',w'}=0$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]], [[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]).

[F5] **States of the model.** $T_{\psi,\psi}$ for $\|\psi\|=1$ is a state; a convex combination of states is a state ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] clause (a), [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)).

## Proof

1.1 [Clause (a): certainty] By [F1] the orthogonal projection $P=E_{A}(\{\lambda\})$ has range $K$ and acts as the identity on $K$, so $P\psi=\psi$ and $\|P\psi\|^{2}=1$. The outcome law [F2] gives $p_{\lambda}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P)=\|P\psi\|^{2}=1>0$, and the conditional state is $\rho_{\lambda}=P\rho P/p_{\lambda}=P T_{\psi,\psi}P=T_{P\psi,P\psi}=T_{\psi,\psi}=\rho$ by [F3] and the rank-one rule $PT_{\psi,\psi}P=T_{P\psi,P\psi}$ [F4]. This is (a). [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

2.1 [Clause (b): unchanged laws] Fix an assigned sharp observable $C$ and a Borel set $S$. By [F2] its outcome law in the conditional state is $\mu^{C}_{\rho_{\lambda}}(S)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{\lambda}E_{C}(S))$; since $\rho_{\lambda}=\rho$ by step 1.1, this equals $\mu^{C}_{\rho}(S)$ for every $S$ and every $C$. No operation on the state separates the two computations, so the $\lambda$-readout induces no change within the eigenspace. This is (b). [step 1.1, F2, algebra]

2.2 [Clause (c): the coherence witness] Let $\psi=\alpha u+\beta v$ with $u,v$ orthonormal in $K$; then $P\psi=\psi$ and step 1.1 gives $\rho_{\lambda}=T_{\psi,\psi}$. The vectors $w=(u+v)/\sqrt2$ and $w'=(u-v)/\sqrt2$ are orthonormal, and $W=T_{w,w}-T_{w',w'}$ is bounded and self-adjoint with $Ww=w$, $Ww'=-w'$, so $T_{w,w}$ and $T_{w',w'}$ are its spectral projections at $+1$ and $-1$ and the value $0$ has projection $I-T_{w,w}-T_{w',w'}$ [F4]. For $\alpha=\beta=1/\sqrt2$ one has $\psi=w$, so by [F2] the conditional state assigns to the value $+1$ of $W$ the probability $\operatorname{tr}(T_{w,w}T_{w,w})=1$, while the mixture $\sigma=|\alpha|^{2}T_{u,u}+|\beta|^{2}T_{v,v}$ assigns to $+1$ the probability $|\alpha|^{2}\operatorname{tr}(T_{u,u}T_{w,w})+|\beta|^{2}\operatorname{tr}(T_{v,v}T_{w,w})=\tfrac12|\langle u,w\rangle|^{2}+\tfrac12|\langle v,w\rangle|^{2}=\tfrac12(\tfrac12+\tfrac12)=\tfrac12$, and to $-1$ the remaining probability $\tfrac12$; the two preparations therefore have different laws for the assigned sharp observable $W$. This is (c). [step 1.1, given, F2, F4, F5, algebra]

3.1 [Clause (d) and scope] The update used in steps 1.1-3.1 is the adopted Lueders update with $P=E_{A}(\{\lambda\})$ [F1, F2]; declarations with a finer family inside $K$ are different declared measurements and are not evaluated here, and no apparatus that realizes the $\lambda$-readout is asserted. This is (d). [step 2.2, given, F1, F2, algebra] ∎

references.title: D. Tong, Quantum Mechanics (author-hosted lecture set), Section 3.3, printed pages 76-77 (degenerate spectrum: outcome probability as the sum of |a_n|^2 and collapse to the normalized superposition inside the eigenspace)

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 1.4, printed page 15 (ideal measurement leaves the system in a state certain to yield the recorded value) and Section 7.4.2, printed pages 161-164 (successive measurements and their order dependence)

items.physical_scope: A conditional statement about the declared ideal sharp measurement of a bounded assigned sharp observable at a degenerate eigenvalue: the Lueders update by the eigenspace projection leaves a pure preparation inside that eigenspace unchanged, so no decoherence is induced inside the eigenspace and subsequent laws are those of the unmodified preparation. It asserts no apparatus realization and does not claim that a laboratory eigenvalue readout preserves coherence or that it resolves or fails to resolve the degeneracy in any particular device.

items.title: Outcome effects do not determine the conditional update, and general instruments need not be repeatable
items.statement:
Adopt the state postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2 and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate P3 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]]), and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let a declared two-level system have state space $D(\mathbb C^{2})$ with orthonormal basis $(e_{1},e_{2})$ of $\mathbb C^{2}$ ([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]), write $P_{i}:=T_{e_{i},e_{i}}$ for the rank-one projections and $W:=T_{e_{2},e_{1}}+T_{e_{1},e_{2}}$ for the swap, and put $B:=P_{1}-P_{2}$. Then:

**(a) Two normalized instruments with equal effects.** The families
$$\bigl(M_{0},M_{1}\bigr)=\bigl(P_{1},P_{2}\bigr),\qquad \bigl(M_{0}',M_{1}'\bigr)=\bigl(WP_{1},P_{2}\bigr)$$
are both normalized declared instruments on $\mathbb C^{2}$, and both have the effects $F_{0}=F_{0}'=P_{1}$, $F_{1}=F_{1}'=P_{2}$.

**(b) Different updates and different predictions.** For every state $\rho$ with $p_{0}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{1})>0$ the conditional state after the outcome $0$ is $T_{e_{1},e_{1}}$ for the first instrument and $T_{e_{2},e_{2}}$ for the second. Consequently, for the bounded assigned sharp observable $B=P_{1}-P_{2}$, the probability of the value $+1$ after the outcome $0$ is $1$ under the first instrument and $0$ under the second, although the two instruments have identical outcome effects and identical outcome probabilities $p_{0},p_{1}$ in every preparation. Hence the effects do not determine the conditional update; the update is part of the declared apparatus model (clause (v) of P3, [[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]] clause (d)).

**(c) A non-repeatable declared instrument.** The family
$$N_{+}:=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}I,\qquad N_{-}:=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}B$$
is a normalized declared instrument with effects $F_{+}=F_{-}=\tfrac12 I$. Its outcome probabilities are $\tfrac12,\tfrac12$ in every preparation, and conditioned on either outcome an immediate repetition of the same declared instrument again yields each outcome with probability $\tfrac12$; the probability of repeating the same outcome is $\tfrac12$, not $1$. So declared instruments need not be repeatable, in contrast to the projective Lueders case of [[pthm-nrqm-measurement-projective-outcomes-and-discarded-ensembles]] clause (b).

**(d) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) are statements about the declared instruments displayed; they assert no property of any laboratory device, no uniqueness of recorded outcomes and no dynamics of an apparatus. Whether a device is described by one of these instruments is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The adopted postulates P1, P2, P3; the two-level space $\mathbb C^{2}$ with orthonormal basis $(e_{1},e_{2})$; the rank-one projections $P_{1}=T_{e_{1},e_{1}}$, $P_{2}=T_{e_{2},e_{2}}$; the swap $W=T_{e_{2},e_{1}}+T_{e_{1},e_{2}}$; the operator $B=P_{1}-P_{2}$; the Kraus families of clauses (a) and (c); a state $\rho$.

[F1] **Rank-one calculus and two-level algebra.** $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ is bounded with $T_{u,v}T_{x,y}=\langle x,v\rangle T_{u,y}$ and $T_{u,v}^{*}=T_{v,u}$; for orthonormal $u,v$, $T_{u,u}$ and $T_{v,v}$ are orthogonal projections with $T_{u,u}+T_{v,v}=I$ on the span, $T_{u,u}T_{v,v}=0$, and $\operatorname{tr}(T_{u,u}S)=\langle Su,u\rangle$ for trace-class $S$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]], [[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]).

[F2] **Declared instruments.** A normalized finite Kraus family $(M_{a,r})$ with $\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}=I$ declares an instrument with effects $F_{a}=\sum_{r}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}$, outcome probabilities $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$ and conditional updates $\rho\mapsto p_{a}^{-1}\sum_{r}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}$ for $p_{a}>0$; the update is part of the declaration and is not determined by the effects ([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]] clause (d), clause (iv) of [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], clause (v) of [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]]).

[F3] **Abstract non-determination.** There are two normalized instruments on $\mathbb C^{2}$ with the same outcome effects whose updates differ on the same input; effects alone do not determine the update ([[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]] clause (d)).

[F4] **Projective updates are repeatable.** For a declared ideal sharp measurement, the conditional state after outcome $a$ returns $a$ with certainty on immediate repetition ([[pthm-nrqm-measurement-projective-outcomes-and-discarded-ensembles]] clause (b)).

[F5] **States.** $T_{\psi,\psi}$ with $\|\psi\|=1$ is a state, and $\operatorname{tr}(T_{u,u}S)=\langle Su,u\rangle$ for bounded self-adjoint $S$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], [F1]).

## Proof

1.1 [Normalization of the first two instruments] For the first family, $M_{0}^{*}M_{0}=P_{1}^{2}=P_{1}$ and $M_{1}^{*}M_{1}=P_{2}$, so $M_{0}^{*}M_{0}+M_{1}^{*}M_{1}=P_{1}+P_{2}=I$ [F1]. For the second, $M_{0}^{\prime*}=P_{1}W^{*}$ gives $M_{0}^{\prime*}M_{0}'=P_{1}W^{*}WP_{1}=P_{1}^{2}=P_{1}$ because $W^{*}W=I$, and $M_{1}^{\prime*}M_{1}'=P_{2}$; again the sum is $I$. Both families are therefore normalized declared instruments [F2] with the displayed effects $F_{0}=P_{1}$, $F_{1}=P_{2}$ and $F_{0}'=P_{1}$, $F_{1}'=P_{2}$. This is (a). [given, F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 [Equal outcome probabilities] Since the effects of the two instruments coincide, for every state $\rho$ and each outcome the probability is $p_{0}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{1})$ or $p_{1}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{2})$ with the same value under either instrument [F2]; in particular $p_{0}+p_{1}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(P_{1}+P_{2}))=1$. [step 1.1, F2, algebra]

2.2 [Non-repeatability] For the family of clause (c), $N_{+}^{*}N_{+}=\tfrac12I$ and $N_{-}^{*}N_{-}=\tfrac12B^{2}=\tfrac12I$ by $B^{2}=P_{1}+P_{2}=I$ [F1], so the family is normalized [F2] with effects $F_{+}=F_{-}=\tfrac12I$ and outcome probabilities $\tfrac12,\tfrac12$ in every preparation by [F2]. If the outcome $+$ occurs, the conditional state is $\tfrac12\rho/\tfrac12=\rho$, so the probability that an immediate repetition returns $+$ is again $\operatorname{tr}(\rho\cdot\tfrac12I)=\tfrac12$; if the outcome $-$ occurs, the conditional state is $(\tfrac12B\rho B)/(\tfrac12)=B\rho B$, and the probability that the repetition returns $-$ is $\operatorname{tr}(B\rho B\cdot\tfrac12I)=\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(B^{2}\rho)=\tfrac12$. Hence the probability of repeating the same outcome is $\tfrac12$ in both cases, not $1$; the declared instrument is not repeatable. This is (c), and it is consistent with the repeatability of the projective case [F4] because $N_{\pm}$ are not projections. [step 1.1, F1, F2, F4, algebra]

3.1 [Different conditional updates] Let $\rho$ be a state with $p_{0}>0$. For the first instrument, $M_{0}\rho M_{0}^{*}=P_{1}\rho P_{1}$, and evaluating in the eigen-expansion of $\rho$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)) or directly by [F1] gives $P_{1}\rho P_{1}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{1})P_{1}=p_{0}P_{1}$; hence the conditional state is $P_{1}=T_{e_{1},e_{1}}$. For the second, $M_{0}'\rho M_{0}^{\prime*}=WP_{1}\rho P_{1}W^{*}=p_{0}WP_{1}W^{*}=p_{0}T_{e_{2},e_{2}}$ by [F1] and $We_{1}=e_{2}$; hence the conditional state is $T_{e_{2},e_{2}}$. The two updates differ, while step 2.1 gives equal outcome probabilities. [step 1.1, step 2.1, F1, F2, algebra]

4.1 [Different subsequent predictions] The observable $B=P_{1}-P_{2}$ is bounded and self-adjoint with spectral projections $P_{1}$ at $+1$ and $P_{2}$ at $-1$, so the probability of the value $+1$ in a preparation $\sigma$ is $\operatorname{tr}(\sigma P_{1})$. In the conditional state $T_{e_{1},e_{1}}$ of the first instrument this is $\operatorname{tr}(T_{e_{1},e_{1}}P_{1})=1$ by [F1], and in the conditional state $T_{e_{2},e_{2}}$ of the second it is $\operatorname{tr}(T_{e_{2},e_{2}}P_{1})=|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle|^{2}=0$. Thus instruments with the same effects make different predictions for a subsequent measurement, which proves (b). [step 3.1, F1, F5, algebra]

5.1 [Scope] Steps 1.1-5.1 are computations inside the declared instruments of clauses (a) and (c) using the adopted P2(iv) and P3(v) through [F2]; they assert no device behaviour and no outcome uniqueness. This is (d). [step 2.2, F2, F3, algebra] ∎

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 1.3.6 and 1.4, printed pages 14-15 (photon analyzers and ideal measurement)

The theorem is a statement about declared apparatus models under P2(iv) and P3(v); it asserts no apparatus realization and no empirical fact.

items.title: A declared finite effect family is realised by a dilated ideal projective measurement
items.statement:
Adopt the state postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2 and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate P3 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]]), and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice. Let $H$ be the nonzero complex Hilbert space assigned to a declared system, and let $(F_{a})_{a=1}^{n}$ be a declared finite family of effects on $H$: bounded operators with $0\le F_{a}\le I$ and $\sum_{a}F_{a}=I$ ([[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]], clause (iv) of P2). Let $C=\mathbb C^{n}$ with orthonormal basis $(e_{a})_{a=1}^{n}$, form the completed tensor product $H\widehat\otimes C$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), and define
$$W:H\to H\widehat\otimes C,\qquad W\psi:=\sum_{a=1}^{n}F_{a}^{1/2}\psi\otimes e_{a},\qquad P_{a}:=I_{H}\otimes T_{e_{a},e_{a}},$$
where $F_{a}^{1/2}$ is the positive square root supplied by the continuous functional calculus ([[thm-continuous-functional-calculus-for-bounded-self-adjoint-operators]]) and $T_{x,x}$ is the rank-one projection of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]. Then:

**(a) The dilation.** $W$ is a linear isometry, the operators $P_{a}$ are pairwise orthogonal orthogonal projections on $H\widehat\otimes C$ with strong sum $I$, and $W^{*}P_{a}W=F_{a}$ for every $a$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-naimark-compression]]).

**(b) Realised outcome probabilities.** For every state $\rho$ on $H$ the operator $\widetilde\rho:=W\rho W^{*}$ is a state on $H\widehat\otimes C$, and the declared ideal sharp measurement $(P_{a})_{a=1}^{n}$ on the composite model space has outcome probabilities
$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\widetilde\rho\,P_{a}\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})\qquad(a=1,\dots,n).$$

**(c) The induced instrument.** Let $\Lambda$ be the trace-preserving map $\Lambda(\sigma)=\sum_{b=1}^{n}F_{b}^{1/2}\sigma F_{b}^{1/2}$ (the square-root Kraus map of the effect family). If $p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})>0$, the conditional composite state after the outcome $a$ is $\widetilde\rho_{a}=P_{a}\widetilde\rho P_{a}/p_{a}$, and its reduction to $H$ is the state
$$\operatorname{Tr}_{C}\widetilde\rho_{a}=\frac{1}{p_{a}}\,\Lambda\bigl(F_{a}^{1/2}\rho F_{a}^{1/2}\bigr)=\frac{1}{p_{a}}\sum_{b=1}^{n}F_{b}^{1/2}F_{a}^{1/2}\rho F_{a}^{1/2}F_{b}^{1/2};$$
the non-selective composite state reduces to $\operatorname{Tr}_{C}\sum_{a}P_{a}\widetilde\rho P_{a}=\sum_{b}F_{b}^{1/2}\bigl(\sum_{a}F_{a}^{1/2}\rho F_{a}^{1/2}\bigr)F_{b}^{1/2}=\Lambda^{2}(\rho)$. The instrument that the dilated measurement induces on $H$ is therefore the declared instrument with Kraus family $\bigl(F_{b}^{1/2}F_{a}^{1/2}\bigr)_{a,b}$ and effects $F_{a}$ ([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]] clause (d)).

**(d) Projective case and non-determination.** If the effects are pairwise orthogonal projections, $F_{a}=P_{a}^{\circ}$ with $P_{a}^{\circ}P_{b}^{\circ}=0$ for $a\ne b$, then the induced update of clause (c) is the Lueders update $P_{a}^{\circ}\rho P_{a}^{\circ}/p_{a}$. In general the induced update of clause (c) differs from the square-root Kraus update $F_{a}^{1/2}\rho F_{a}^{1/2}/p_{a}$ of the same effects: for $H=\mathbb C^{2}$ with orthonormal basis $(e_{1},e_{2})$, $F_{1}=\operatorname{diag}(3/4,1/4)$, $F_{2}=I-F_{1}$, $\rho=T_{w,w}$ with $w=(e_{1}+e_{2})/\sqrt2$ and $p_{1}=1/2$, the two conditional states have matrices
$$\frac{1}{p_{1}}\Lambda\bigl(F_{1}^{1/2}\rho F_{1}^{1/2}\bigr)=\begin{pmatrix}3/4&3/8\\3/8&1/4\end{pmatrix},\qquad \frac{1}{p_{1}}F_{1}^{1/2}\rho F_{1}^{1/2}=\begin{pmatrix}3/4&\sqrt3/4\\ \sqrt3/4&1/4\end{pmatrix}.$$
Thus the same effect family is compatible with more than one update, in agreement with [[pthm-nrqm-measurement-instrument-updates-not-determined-by-effects]].

**(e) Scope.** The ancilla register $C$ and the isometry $W$ are mathematical objects of a declared composite model space; the theorem asserts no physical ancilla, no physical realisation of the dilated projective measurement and no preferred outcome. Whether a laboratory device realises the declared effects or either update is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The adopted postulates P1, P2, P3; a nonzero complex Hilbert space $H$; a declared finite effect family $(F_{a})_{a=1}^{n}$ with $\sum_{a}F_{a}=I$; the ancilla $C=\mathbb C^{n}$ with orthonormal basis $(e_{a})$; the isometry $W$ and projections $P_{a}$ of the Statement; a state $\rho$ on $H$.

[F1] **Finite Naimark compression.** $W\psi=\sum_{a}F_{a}^{1/2}\psi\otimes e_{a}$ is a linear isometry, the operators $P_{a}=I_{H}\otimes T_{e_{a},e_{a}}$ are pairwise orthogonal orthogonal projections with $\sum_{a}P_{a}=I$, and $W^{*}P_{a}W=F_{a}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-naimark-compression]]; [[thm-continuous-functional-calculus-for-bounded-self-adjoint-operators]] for the square roots).

[F2] **Tensor and partial-trace rules.** On $H\widehat\otimes C$ the pairing is $\langle u\otimes c,u'\otimes c'\rangle=\langle u,u'\rangle\langle c,c'\rangle$, bounded operators act as $S\otimes T$ with $(S\otimes T)^{*}=S^{*}\otimes T^{*}$, and the partial trace $\operatorname{Tr}_{C}$ is the trace-preserving positive linear map with $\operatorname{Tr}_{C}(S\otimes T_{c,c'})=\langle c',c\rangle S$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]]); in particular $\operatorname{Tr}_{C}(WXW^{*})=\sum_{b}F_{b}^{1/2}XF_{b}^{1/2}$ for trace-class $X$, because $(I\otimes\langle e_{b}|)W=F_{b}^{1/2}$ and $W^{*}(I\otimes|e_{b}\rangle)=F_{b}^{1/2}$.

[F3] **States and effects.** A density operator is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator of trace one; for effects $0\le F_{a}\le I$ with $\sum_{a}F_{a}=I$ one has $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})\in[0,1]$ and $\sum_{a}p_{a}=1$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a), [[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]] clauses (a)-(b)).

[F4] **Declared instrument.** A normalized Kraus family $(M_{a,b})$ with $\sum_{a,b}M_{a,b}^{*}M_{a,b}=I$ declares an instrument with effects $F_{a}=\sum_{b}M_{a,b}^{*}M_{a,b}$, outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$ and conditional updates $\rho\mapsto p_{a}^{-1}\sum_{b}M_{a,b}\rho M_{a,b}^{*}$ ([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]] clause (d)).

[F5] **Projective Lueders case.** If the effects are pairwise orthogonal projections, the update $F_{a}^{1/2}\rho F_{a}^{1/2}/p_{a}$ equals the Lueders update $F_{a}\rho F_{a}/p_{a}$ because $F_{a}^{1/2}=F_{a}$ for a projection ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], [[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]).

## Proof

1.1 [Clause (a)] The isometry, the projection family and the compression identity $W^{*}P_{a}W=F_{a}$ are exactly the conclusions of [F1] under the present hypotheses (bounded effects, $\sum_{a}F_{a}=I$, finite ancilla). This is (a). [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 [The dilated state and the outcome probabilities] Since $W$ is an isometry, $W^{*}W=I_{H}$ and $\operatorname{tr}(W\rho W^{*})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho W^{*}W)=\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$; $W\rho W^{*}$ is positive because $\rho$ is positive and $W$ is linear, and it is trace class as a product of bounded and trace-class factors [F2]; hence $\widetilde\rho$ is a state [F3]. For each $a$, $\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho P_{a})=\operatorname{tr}(W\rho W^{*}P_{a})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho W^{*}P_{a}W)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$ by [F1] and cyclicity of the trace. This is (b). [step 1.1, given, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

3.1 [The induced conditional state] Assume $p_{a}>0$. The conditional composite state is $\widetilde\rho_{a}=P_{a}\widetilde\rho P_{a}/p_{a}$ by [F4] (with the projections $P_{a}$ as the Kraus family of the composite measurement). Since $P_{a}W=WF_{a}^{1/2}$ by $P_{a}W\psi=(I\otimes T_{e_{a},e_{a}})\sum_{b}F_{b}^{1/2}\psi\otimes e_{b}=F_{a}^{1/2}\psi\otimes e_{a}=WF_{a}^{1/2}\psi$ [F1], one has $P_{a}\widetilde\rho P_{a}=WF_{a}^{1/2}\rho F_{a}^{1/2}W^{*}$, and applying the partial-trace rule of [F2] to $X=F_{a}^{1/2}\rho F_{a}^{1/2}$ gives $\operatorname{Tr}_{C}\widetilde\rho_{a}=\frac{1}{p_{a}}\sum_{b}F_{b}^{1/2}F_{a}^{1/2}\rho F_{a}^{1/2}F_{b}^{1/2}=\Lambda\bigl(F_{a}^{1/2}\rho F_{a}^{1/2}\bigr)/p_{a}$; this is a state because it is the partial trace of the state $\widetilde\rho_{a}$ [F2, F3]. For the non-selective map, $\sum_{a}P_{a}\widetilde\rho P_{a}=W\bigl(\sum_{a}F_{a}^{1/2}\rho F_{a}^{1/2}\bigr)W^{*}$ and another application of the partial-trace rule gives $\sum_{b}F_{b}^{1/2}\bigl(\sum_{a}F_{a}^{1/2}\rho F_{a}^{1/2}\bigr)F_{b}^{1/2}=\Lambda^{2}(\rho)$. The resulting instrument on $H$ has Kraus family $M_{a,b}:=F_{b}^{1/2}F_{a}^{1/2}$: indeed $\sum_{a,b}M_{a,b}^{*}M_{a,b}=\sum_{a,b}F_{a}^{1/2}F_{b}F_{a}^{1/2}=\sum_{a}F_{a}^{1/2}F_{a}^{1/2}=I$, its $a$-th effect is $\sum_{b}F_{a}^{1/2}F_{b}F_{a}^{1/2}=F_{a}$, and its update is the displayed expression, in agreement with [F4]. This is (c). [step 2.1, F1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

4.1 [Projective case] If $F_{a}=P_{a}^{\circ}$ is a projection, then $F_{a}^{1/2}=F_{a}$ and $F_{b}^{1/2}F_{a}^{1/2}=P_{b}^{\circ}P_{a}^{\circ}=\delta_{ab}P_{a}^{\circ}$ for the pairwise orthogonal family; hence the induced update of step 3.1 reduces to $P_{a}^{\circ}\rho P_{a}^{\circ}/p_{a}$, the Lueders update [F5]. [step 3.1, given, F5, algebra]

4.2 [Explicit non-coincidence of the two updates] Take $H=\mathbb C^{2}$ with orthonormal basis $(e_{1},e_{2})$, $F_{1}=\operatorname{diag}(3/4,1/4)$, $F_{2}=I-F_{1}=\operatorname{diag}(1/4,3/4)$ and $\rho=T_{w,w}$ with $w=(e_{1}+e_{2})/\sqrt2$; then $p_{1}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{1})=\tfrac12$ and, writing $a=\sqrt3/2$ and $b=1/2$ for the diagonal entries of $F_{1}^{1/2}=\operatorname{diag}(a,b)$ and $F_{2}^{1/2}=\operatorname{diag}(b,a)$, a direct matrix computation gives $F_{1}^{1/2}\rho F_{1}^{1/2}=\tfrac12\begin{pmatrix}3/4&\sqrt3/4\\ \sqrt3/4&1/4\end{pmatrix}$ and $\Lambda\bigl(F_{1}^{1/2}\rho F_{1}^{1/2}\bigr)=\tfrac12\begin{pmatrix}3/4&3/8\\3/8&1/4\end{pmatrix}$; after division by $p_{1}=1/2$ the induced conditional state of step 3.1 is $\begin{pmatrix}3/4&3/8\\3/8&1/4\end{pmatrix}$ while the square-root Kraus update is $\begin{pmatrix}3/4&\sqrt3/4\\ \sqrt3/4&1/4\end{pmatrix}$, which are distinct because $3/8\ne\sqrt3/4$ and both are unit-trace positive semidefinite matrices, the second of rank one. Hence the effects $F_{1},F_{2}$ do not determine the update, in agreement with [[pthm-nrqm-measurement-instrument-updates-not-determined-by-effects]]. This is (d). [step 3.1, given, F4, F5, algebra]

5.1 [Scope] The preceding steps were carried out entirely in the declared composite model space $H\widehat\otimes C$ with the mathematical ancilla $C$; no physical ancilla, apparatus or outcome selection was used. This is (e). [step 4.2, given, F1, F2, algebra] ∎

items.title: Declared countable instruments: normalization, discarded ensembles and the repeatability criterion
items.statement:
Adopt the state postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2 and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate P3 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]]), and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, the hypothesis of the cited mathematics. Let $H$ be the nonzero complex Hilbert space assigned to a declared system ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]), and let $(M_{a})_{a\ge1}$ be a declared normalized countable Kraus family on $H$: bounded operators with
$$\sum_{a=1}^{N}M_{a}^{*}M_{a}\longrightarrow I\qquad\text{strongly as }N\to\infty .$$
Declare the countable instrument with outcome set $\{1,2,\dots\}$, effects $F_{a}:=M_{a}^{*}M_{a}$, outcome probabilities $p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$, conditional updates $\rho_{a}:=M_{a}\rho M_{a}^{*}/p_{a}$ for $p_{a}>0$, and discarded-outcome map $\Phi(\rho):=\sum_{a\ge1}M_{a}\rho M_{a}^{*}$ ([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]] clause (d)). Then:

**(a) POVM and discarded ensemble.** Each $F_{a}$ is an effect, $0\le F_{a}\le I$; for every state $\rho$ one has $p_{a}\ge0$ and $\sum_{a}p_{a}=1$; $\Phi$ is a positive trace-preserving linear map of the trace-class operators and maps states to states; and $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\rho_{a}$, a trace-norm convergent mixture of the conditional states.

**(b) Repeatability criterion.** The declared instrument is **repeatable**, i.e. for every state $\rho$ and every $a$ with $p_{a}>0$ an immediate repetition of the same declared instrument returns the outcome $a$ with probability $1$ and every $b\ne a$ with probability $0$, if and only if
$$M_{b}M_{a}=0\quad(b\ne a),\qquad F_{a}^{2}=F_{a}\quad\text{for every }a\text{ with }F_{a}\ne0 .$$

**(c) Projective case.** For a declared ideal sharp measurement $(P_{a})$ the Kraus family $M_{a}=P_{a}$ satisfies the criterion of (b) and is repeatable, in agreement with [[pthm-nrqm-measurement-projective-outcomes-and-discarded-ensembles]] clause (b); a general normalized Kraus family need not satisfy it ([[pthm-nrqm-measurement-instrument-updates-not-determined-by-effects]] clause (c)).

**(d) Non-determination.** The effects $(F_{a})$ determine the outcome probabilities but not the conditional updates; the Kraus family is part of the declared instrument (clause (v) of P3, [[pthm-nrqm-measurement-instrument-updates-not-determined-by-effects]] clause (b)).

**(e) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(d) are conditional statements about the declared countable instrument; they assert no apparatus realization, no outcome uniqueness and no empirical fact, and no claim is made that every positive trace-preserving map admits such a Kraus family ([[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]] clause (c)).

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The adopted postulates P1, P2, P3; a normalized countable Kraus family $(M_{a})_{a\ge1}$ on $H$; its effects $F_{a}=M_{a}^{*}M_{a}$, probabilities $p_{a}$, updates $\rho_{a}$ and discarded map $\Phi$; a state $\rho$.

[F1] **Countable Kraus normalization.** For a bounded family with $\sum_{a\le N}M_{a}^{*}M_{a}\to I$ strongly: $\sum_{a}\|M_{a}x\|^{2}=\|x\|^{2}$ for every $x$; for every positive trace-class $\rho$ the series $\sum_{a}M_{a}\rho M_{a}^{*}$ converges in trace norm to a positive trace-class operator with trace $\operatorname{tr}\rho$; the map extends uniquely to a linear positive trace-preserving map of the trace-class operators and carries states to states ([[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]] clauses (a)-(c)).

[F2] **Density expansions.** A state has an expansion $\rho=\sum_{n}w_{n}T_{u_{n},u_{n}}$ with orthonormal $(u_{n})$, $w_{n}\ge0$, $\sum_{n}w_{n}=1$; then $\operatorname{tr}(\rho B)=\sum_{n}w_{n}\langle Bu_{n},u_{n}\rangle$ for bounded $B$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a), [[lem-nrqm-composites-nuclear-bounded-cyclicity]] clause (b)).

[F3] **Positivity of the Kraus products.** $F_{a}=M_{a}^{*}M_{a}\ge0$ and $F_{a}\le I$: the finite sums $G_{N}:=\sum_{a\le N}F_{a}$ satisfy $0\le G_{N}\le G_{N+1}\le I$ because $G_{N+1}-G_{N}=F_{N+1}\ge0$ and $\langle(I-G_{N})x,x\rangle=\sum_{a>N}\|M_{a}x\|^{2}\to0$ ([[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]] clause (b), [F1]).

[F4] **Zero quadratic form.** If $X$ is a positive bounded operator and $\langle Xu,u\rangle=0$ for every unit vector $u$, then $X=0$: by Cauchy-Schwarz for the positive semidefinite sesquilinear form $(x,y)\mapsto\langle Xx,y\rangle$ one has $|\langle Xx,y\rangle|^{2}\le\langle Xx,x\rangle\langle Xy,y\rangle=0$ for all $x,y$ ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-in-an-inner-product-space]], [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]).

[F5] **Updates and their formulas.** For $p_{a}>0$ one has $\rho_{a}=M_{a}\rho M_{a}^{*}/p_{a}$ with $\operatorname{tr}(M_{a}\rho M_{a}^{*})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})=p_{a}$ ([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]] clause (d), [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] clause (e), [[lem-nrqm-composites-nuclear-bounded-cyclicity]] clause (b)).

## Proof

1.1 [The effects and the probabilities] By [F3] each $F_{a}$ is an effect. For a state $\rho$ with expansion [F2], $\sum_{a}p_{a}=\sum_{a}\sum_{n}w_{n}\|M_{a}u_{n}\|^{2}=\sum_{n}w_{n}\|u_{n}\|^{2}=1$ by [F1] with $x=u_{n}$ and $\sum_{n}w_{n}=1$; all terms are nonnegative, so the interchange of the sums is legitimate and $p_{a}\ge0$ for each $a$. [given, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 [The discarded map and the mixture identity] By [F1] the series $\sum_{a}M_{a}\rho M_{a}^{*}$ converges in trace norm, its sum $\Phi(\rho)$ is positive trace class with trace $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$, and $\Phi$ is trace preserving; hence $\Phi(\rho)$ is a state [F1, F2]. For a label with $p_{a}=0$, [F5] gives $\operatorname{tr}(M_{a}\rho M_{a}^{*})=p_{a}=0$, so the positive trace-class summand $M_{a}\rho M_{a}^{*}$ is $0$; therefore the nonzero summands are exactly those with $p_{a}>0$, and $M_{a}\rho M_{a}^{*}=p_{a}\rho_{a}$ for them [F5]. Reindexing the trace-norm convergent series gives $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\rho_{a}$. This is (a). [step 1.1, F1, F2, F5, algebra]

3.1 [Sufficiency of the criterion] Assume $M_{b}M_{a}=0$ for $b\ne a$ and $F_{a}^{2}=F_{a}$ whenever $F_{a}\ne0$. Fix a state $\rho$ and $a$ with $p_{a}>0$, and let $\rho_{a}$ be the conditional state. Then $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})>0$ forces $F_{a}\ne0$, and the probability that the immediate repetition returns $a$ is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}F_{a})=\operatorname{tr}(M_{a}\rho M_{a}^{*}F_{a})/p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho M_{a}^{*}F_{a}M_{a})/p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a}^{2})/p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})/p_{a}=1$, using $M_{a}^{*}F_{a}M_{a}=M_{a}^{*}M_{a}^{*}M_{a}M_{a}=(F_{a})^{2}$ and [F5]. For $b\ne a$, $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}F_{b})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho M_{a}^{*}M_{b}^{*}M_{b}M_{a})/p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho (M_{b}M_{a})^{*}(M_{b}M_{a}))/p_{a}=0$ by $M_{b}M_{a}=0$. Hence the instrument is repeatable. [step 2.1, given, F1, F5, algebra]

4.1 [Necessity of the criterion] Conversely assume the instrument repeatable. Fix $a$ with $F_{a}\ne0$; since $\langle F_{a}u,u\rangle=\|M_{a}u\|^{2}$ is not identically zero, there is a unit vector $u$ with $p_{a}(T_{u,u})>0$, so a state $\sigma$ with $p_{a}(\sigma)>0$ exists. For such a $\sigma$ and $b\ne a$, repeatability gives $0=\operatorname{tr}(\sigma_{a}F_{b})=\operatorname{tr}(\sigma\,(M_{b}M_{a})^{*}(M_{b}M_{a}))/p_{a}(\sigma)$, hence $\operatorname{tr}(\sigma X)=0$ for the positive bounded operator $X:=(M_{b}M_{a})^{*}(M_{b}M_{a})$; for an arbitrary state $\rho'$ and $t\in(0,1]$ the convex combination $\rho_{t}=(1-t)\sigma+t\rho'$ again has $p_{a}(\rho_{t})>0$, so $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{t}X)=0$; subtracting the known identity $\operatorname{tr}(\sigma X)=0$ and dividing by $t$ gives $\operatorname{tr}(\rho'X)=0$ for every state $\rho'$, in particular $\langle Xu,u\rangle=0$ for every unit $u$, so $X=0$ by [F4], that is $M_{b}M_{a}=0$ for all $b\ne a$. Similarly, repeatability for the outcome $a$ itself gives $1=\operatorname{tr}(\sigma_{a}F_{a})=\operatorname{tr}(\sigma F_{a}^{2})/p_{a}(\sigma)$, that is $\operatorname{tr}(\sigma(F_{a}-F_{a}^{2}))=0$; applying the same convex-combination subtraction to the self-adjoint operator $F_{a}-F_{a}^{2}$ gives $\operatorname{tr}(\rho'(F_{a}-F_{a}^{2}))=0$ for every state $\rho'$, and since $0\le F_{a}\le I$ implies $F_{a}-F_{a}^{2}=F_{a}(I-F_{a})\ge0$, [F4] yields $F_{a}-F_{a}^{2}=0$, that is $F_{a}^{2}=F_{a}$. This proves the criterion. [step 3.1, given, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, algebra]

5.1 [Clauses (c) and (d)] For a declared ideal sharp measurement, $M_{a}=P_{a}$ satisfies $M_{b}M_{a}=P_{b}P_{a}=\delta_{ab}P_{a}$ and $F_{a}=P_{a}^{2}=P_{a}$, so the criterion of (b) holds and the instrument is repeatable, in agreement with [[pthm-nrqm-measurement-projective-outcomes-and-discarded-ensembles]] clause (b); the explicit instrument of [[pthm-nrqm-measurement-instrument-updates-not-determined-by-effects]] clause (c) violates repeatability, so the criterion is not automatic. Since the outcome probabilities are functions of the effects alone while distinct normalized Kraus families may share effects, the effects do not determine the update; this is the non-determination recorded in [[pthm-nrqm-measurement-instrument-updates-not-determined-by-effects]] clause (b) and clause (v) of P3. This is (c) and (d). [step 4.1, given, F1, F3, algebra]

6.1 [Scope] Clauses (a)-(d) were derived from the declared Kraus family and the cited mathematics; no step used a claim about an apparatus, and the converse direction of the criterion did not assume that every positive trace-preserving map has a Kraus family, since the family was declared. This is (e). [step 5.1, given, F1, algebra] ∎

items.title: Scope and empirical status of the measurement-and-instruments page
items.statement:
**Adopted, not derived.** Every measurement statement of this page is conditional on the adopted ideal conditional-measurement postulate P3 ([[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]]), read in the vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]. The Lueders update is not derived from the Born outcome law of P2, and the Born outcome law is not derived from the collapse rule: the two are separate adopted clauses, and the theorems of this page deduce conditional consequences of them and of the cited mathematics. P3 itself records that its declared class is an idealization.

**Declared apparatus models only.** [[pthm-nrqm-measurement-projective-outcomes-and-discarded-ensembles]] states the outcome law, repeatability, the discarded-outcome ensemble and coherence loss for a declared ideal sharp measurement; [[pthm-nrqm-measurement-degenerate-eigenspace-update]] shows that the update by an eigenspace projection preserves coherence inside a degenerate eigenspace; [[pthm-nrqm-measurement-instrument-updates-not-determined-by-effects]] and [[pthm-nrqm-measurement-finite-effects-dilation]] show that a family of outcome effects does not determine the conditional update and that a declared finite effect family admits an ideal dilated projective model; [[pthm-nrqm-measurement-countable-kraus-instruments]] develops declared countable instruments and their repeatability criterion. None of these items asserts that a particular laboratory device realizes the declared measurement, filter or instrument, and none asserts a preferred or unique recorded outcome; the identification of a device with a declared model is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]).

**What is excluded from the declared sharp class.** A measurement of an exact value of a quantity with continuous spectrum is not represented here by normalizing a delta symbol (clauses (iii) of P2 and (v) of P3); a destructive or absorbing detector is not a projective measurement of the incoming system and must be modeled by its own instrument, one instance being the finite instrument of the companion page; and a unitary system-apparatus interaction produces conditional correlations without, by itself, selecting a recorded outcome (clause (v) of P3).

**No empirical content.** No item of this page records a measurement, an apparatus calibration, a count, an uncertainty or a comparison with data. The probabilities computed in this page are model probabilities for declared preparations and declared apparatus models; agreement or disagreement with recorded data would test the combined model and apparatus assumptions and is not asserted anywhere here.

**Deferred measurement topics.** Joint and compatible sharp measurements, their order independence and their joint laws are developed with the uncertainty-and-compatibility content of the category. The spatial Stern-Gerlach force model, the magnetic-field geometry and the detector-position analysis belong to the magnetic-and-detection material and are not derived here. Measurement-model boundaries for Bell-type comparisons and finite-sample statistical qualifications belong to the later Bell-models page. The reported Stern-Gerlach experiments of 1922 and other primary experimental reports remain candidate experiment items that are not asserted by this page.
