items.title: Serial ideal Stern-Gerlach filters: a two-level model computation
items.statement:
Declare a two-level system whose assigned Hilbert space is $H=\mathbb C^{2}$ with the standard inner product and orthonormal basis $(e_{+},e_{-})$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-inner-product-space]], [[def-hilbert-space]]), interpreted as the two eigenstates of the $z$-component of a spin-half degree of freedom. By the spin assignment of P6 with $s=\tfrac12$, the spin operators are $S_{i}=\hbar J_{i}$ with $J_{i}=\tfrac12\sigma_{i}$ for the Pauli matrices in this basis ([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] clause (ii), [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e)).

For a unit vector $n=(\sin\theta,0,\cos\theta)$, $0\le\theta\le\pi$, put
$$u(\theta):=\cos\frac{\theta}{2}\,e_{+}+\sin\frac{\theta}{2}\,e_{-},\qquad v(\theta):=-\sin\frac{\theta}{2}\,e_{+}+\cos\frac{\theta}{2}\,e_{-}.$$
Then $u(\theta)$ and $v(\theta)$ are orthonormal and
$$S_{n}:=n\cdot \mathbf S=\frac{\hbar}{2}(\sin\theta\,\sigma_{x}+\cos\theta\,\sigma_{z}),\qquad S_{n}u(\theta)=\frac{\hbar}{2}u(\theta),\qquad S_{n}v(\theta)=-\frac{\hbar}{2}v(\theta).$$
Declare the **ideal filter** $F(n)$ to be the ideal sharp measurement with the two outcomes $+$ and $-$, whose outcome projections are $T_{u(\theta),u(\theta)}$ and $T_{v(\theta),v(\theta)}$, the spectral projections of $S_{n}$ at $\pm\hbar/2$ ([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]] clause (c), [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]).

The example considers three ideal filters in series, $F_{1}=F(e_{z})$ (so $\theta=0$), $F_{2}=F(n)$ with axis $n$ at angle $\theta$, and $F_{3}=F(m)$ with axis $m=(\sin\varphi,0,\cos\varphi)$, and the initial preparation $\rho_{0}=T_{e_{+},e_{+}}$, the state of a spin-half system with $S_{z}=+\hbar/2$. Then:

**(i)** Through $F_{1}$ the outcome $+$ has probability $1$ and the conditional state is again $\rho_{0}$.

**(ii)** Through $F_{2}$, conditioned on having passed $F_{1}$,
$$\mathbb P(+)=\cos^{2}\frac{\theta}{2},\qquad \mathbb P(-)=\sin^{2}\frac{\theta}{2},$$
and after the outcome $+$ the conditional state is the pure state of $u(\theta)$.

**(iii)** Through $F_{3}$, conditioned on having passed $F_{2}$ with the outcome $+$, the outcome $+$ has probability
$$\mathbb P(+)=\Bigl|\langle u(\varphi),u(\theta)\rangle\Bigr|^{2}=\cos^{2}\frac{\varphi-\theta}{2}.$$
Hence the joint probability of the outcomes $+,+,+$ is $\cos^{2}(\theta/2)\cos^{2}((\varphi-\theta)/2)$.

**(iv)** In particular, for $\theta=\pi/2$ and $\varphi=\pi$ the filter $F_{2}$ passes half of the atoms that reach it, the filter $F_{3}$ passes half of those, and the joint probability of passing all three filters is $\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac12=\tfrac14$, although without $F_{2}$ in the beam the filter $F_{3}$ would pass none of the atoms emerging from $F_{1}$: $\cos^{2}(\pi/2)=0$. The intervening declared measurement changes the statistics of the later one.

The computation is a model computation for declared ideal filters and the declared spin assignment: it does not derive the spatial Stern-Gerlach deflection or the inhomogeneous-field geometry, records no detector counts, resolution, background or uncertainty, and asserts nothing about the historical silver-atom experiments or about any particular apparatus.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The two-level Hilbert space $H=\mathbb C^{2}$ with orthonormal basis $(e_{+},e_{-})$; the spin-half operators $S_{i}=\hbar J_{i}$; unit vectors $n=(\sin\theta,0,\cos\theta)$, $m=(\sin\varphi,0,\cos\varphi)$; the vectors $u(\theta),v(\theta),u(\varphi),v(\varphi)$; the declared filters $F_{1},F_{2},F_{3}$; the preparation $\rho_{0}=T_{e_{+},e_{+}}$.

[F1] **Spin-half representation.** For $s=\tfrac12$ the matrices of $J_{x},J_{y},J_{z}$ in the basis $(e_{+},e_{-})$ are $\tfrac12\sigma_{x},\tfrac12\sigma_{y},\tfrac12\sigma_{z}$ with $\sigma_{x}=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, $\sigma_{z}=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$, and $S_{i}=\hbar J_{i}$ are self-adjoint ([[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e), [[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] clause (ii)).

[F2] **Spectral projections.** The vectors $u(\theta),v(\theta)$ are orthonormal, span $H$, and satisfy $S_{n}u(\theta)=\tfrac{\hbar}{2}u(\theta)$, $S_{n}v(\theta)=-\tfrac{\hbar}{2}v(\theta)$; hence $T_{u(\theta),u(\theta)}$ and $T_{v(\theta),v(\theta)}$ are the spectral projections of the bounded self-adjoint operator $S_{n}$ at the eigenvalues $\pm\hbar/2$ ([[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] clause (c)).

[F3] **Outcome law and update.** For a declared ideal sharp measurement with projections $P_{a}$ the probability of the outcome $a$ in a state $\rho$ is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})=\|P_{a}\psi\|^{2}$ for a pure preparation $[\psi]$, and the conditional state after a positive-probability outcome is $\rho_{a}=P_{a}\rho P_{a}/p_{a}$ ([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]] clauses (a)-(b), [[pthm-nrqm-measurement-projective-outcomes-and-discarded-ensembles]] clauses (a)-(b)).

[F4] **Rank-one pairing.** $T_{u,u}x=\langle x,u\rangle u$, so $\operatorname{tr}(T_{x,x}T_{u,u})=|\langle x,u\rangle|^{2}$ for unit $x,u$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] clauses (b)-(c)).

[F5] **Elementary overlaps.** For real angles, $\langle u(\varphi),u(\theta)\rangle=\cos\frac{\varphi}{2}\cos\frac{\theta}{2}+\sin\frac{\varphi}{2}\sin\frac{\theta}{2}=\cos\frac{\varphi-\theta}{2}$, and $\langle u(0),u(\theta)\rangle=\cos\frac{\theta}{2}$ ([[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]], [[cor-inner-product-induces-a-norm]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct; compute the spectral projections, probabilities and conditional states on the explicit two-dimensional data.

1.1 [The filter $F_{1}$ and clause (i)] For $\theta=0$ the vectors are $u(0)=e_{+}$, $v(0)=e_{-}$, and $P_{+}=T_{e_{+},e_{+}}$; by [F3] and [F4], $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{0}P_{+})=|\langle e_{+},e_{+}\rangle|^{2}=1$, and the conditional state after the outcome $+$ is $P_{+}\rho_{0}P_{+}/1=T_{e_{+},e_{+}}=\rho_{0}$. This is (i). [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

2.1 [Clause (ii)] By [F2] the projections of $F_{2}$ are $T_{u(\theta),u(\theta)}$ and $T_{v(\theta),v(\theta)}$; [F3] and [F4] give $\mathbb P(+)=\operatorname{tr}(T_{e_{+},e_{+}}T_{u(\theta),u(\theta)})=|\langle e_{+},u(\theta)\rangle|^{2}=\cos^{2}(\theta/2)$ and $\mathbb P(-)=|\langle e_{+},v(\theta)\rangle|^{2}=\sin^{2}(\theta/2)$, the total being $1$. After the outcome $+$ the conditional state is $T_{u(\theta),u(\theta)}$ by [F3] and the rank-one rules, because $T_{u,u}T_{e_{+},e_{+}}T_{u,u}=|\langle e_{+},u\rangle|^{2}T_{u,u}$. This is (ii). [step 1.1, given, F2, F3, F4, F5, algebra]

3.1 [Clause (iii)] The preparation after $F_{2}$ is the pure state of $u(\theta)$, so [F3] and [F4] give $\mathbb P(+)=\operatorname{tr}(T_{u(\theta),u(\theta)}T_{u(\varphi),u(\varphi)})=|\langle u(\theta),u(\varphi)\rangle|^{2}=\cos^{2}((\varphi-\theta)/2)$ by [F5]; multiplying the conditional probabilities of steps 2.1 and 3.1 gives the joint probability $\cos^{2}(\theta/2)\cos^{2}((\varphi-\theta)/2)$ of the outcome sequence $+,+,+$ by the definition of conditional update. This is (iii). [step 2.1, given, F3, F4, F5, algebra]

4.1 [Clause (iv) and scope] Substituting $\theta=\pi/2$ and $\varphi=\pi$ gives $\cos^{2}(\pi/4)=\tfrac12$ for each of the two intermediate steps, hence joint probability $\tfrac14$; without $F_{2}$ the preparation reaching $F_{3}$ would still be $T_{e_{+},e_{+}}$ and the probability of the outcome $+$ at $F_{3}$ would be $|\langle e_{+},u(\pi)\rangle|^{2}=\cos^{2}(\pi/2)=0$, so the presence of the intervening declared measurement changes the later statistics. All quantities computed are model probabilities for the declared filters; no spatial deflection, detector response or measured count was used. This is (iv). [step 3.1, given, F2, F3, F5, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **Idealization.** A physical Stern-Gerlach apparatus separates a beam spatially by the force $\nabla(\boldsymbol\mu\cdot\mathbf B)$ and detects the separated beams; the present example replaces that apparatus by the declared ideal sharp measurement of a spin component. The spatial model, the field profile and the detector-position analysis are separate material and are not claimed here ([[rem-nrqm-measurement-scope-and-empirical-status]]).
- **Order dependence is model-internal.** The statement that inserting $F_{2}$ changes the later statistics is a consequence of the Lueders update for the declared filters; it is not a claim that every physical filter disturbs every subsequent measurement in this way, and it is not a claim about atoms in the absence of a declared preparation and detection model.
- **No empirical content.** The number $\tfrac14$ is an exact model probability for the declared ideal filters, not a measured fraction; no calibration, efficiency, background, alignment or sampling model is supplied.

items.title: Three ideal analysers in series: the quarter-intensity model computation
items.statement:
Declare a two-level system with assigned Hilbert space $H=\mathbb C^{2}$, orthonormal basis $(e_{x},e_{y})$ and standard inner product, as an idealised fixed-mode polarization degree of freedom ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-inner-product-space]], [[def-hilbert-space]]). For a real angle $\alpha$ put
$$e_{\alpha}:=\cos\alpha\,e_{x}+\sin\alpha\,e_{y},\qquad e_{\alpha}^{\perp}:=-\sin\alpha\,e_{x}+\cos\alpha\,e_{y}.$$
The **ideal analyser** $A(\alpha)$ is the declared ideal sharp measurement with the two outcomes transmit and block, whose projections are $T_{e_{\alpha},e_{\alpha}}$ and $T_{e_{\alpha}^{\perp},e_{\alpha}^{\perp}}$ respectively ([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]] clause (c), [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]).

The example takes the preparation $[e_{x}]$, the chain of analysers $A(0)$ with $\alpha=0^\circ$, $A(\pi/4)$ with $\alpha=45^\circ$ and $A(\pi/2)$ with $\alpha=90^\circ$, and computes:

**(i)** The analyser $A(\alpha)$ transmits the preparation $[e_{\beta}]$ with probability
$$\mathbb P(\text{transmit})=\bigl|\langle e_{\alpha},e_{\beta}\rangle\bigr|^{2}=\cos^{2}(\alpha-\beta),$$
and after transmission the conditional state is the pure state of $e_{\alpha}$.

**(ii)** Consequently the chain $0^\circ,45^\circ,90^\circ$ transmits with joint probability
$$\cos^{2}(0-0)\cdot\cos^{2}(\tfrac{\pi}{4}-0)\cdot\cos^{2}(\tfrac{\pi}{2}-\tfrac{\pi}{4})=1\cdot\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac12=\tfrac14 ,$$
whereas the chain $0^\circ,90^\circ$ alone transmits with probability $\cos^{2}(\pi/2)=0$.

**(iii)** Removing the middle analyser therefore changes the transmission of the chain from $0$ to $\tfrac14$ within the declared model: the intervening declared measurement changes the state, and the later analyser sees the state selected by the earlier one, not the original preparation.

**(iv)** *Model comparison only.* A declared classical amplitude model for a transverse field in the same plane, in which the analyser transmits the component along $e_{\alpha}$ and the transmitted intensity is stipulated to be proportional to the squared modulus of that component, gives the same ratio $\cos^{2}(\alpha-\beta)$ for a preparation along $e_{\beta}$. The agreement of these two model computations does not establish that either describes nature, and it does not by itself establish field quantization ([[rem-nrqm-measurement-examples-scope-limits]]); no classical Maxwell theorem is invoked, and the field model is a stipulated finite-dimensional comparison. No transmission counts, detector efficiencies, backgrounds or sampling statistics are reported.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The two-level Hilbert space $H=\mathbb C^{2}$ with orthonormal basis $(e_{x},e_{y})$; real angles $\alpha,\beta$; the unit vectors $e_{\alpha},e_{\alpha}^{\perp},e_{\beta}$; the declared analysers $A(\alpha)$; the pure preparation $[e_{\beta}]$.

[F1] **The analyser is a declared ideal sharp measurement.** $T_{e_{\alpha},e_{\alpha}}$ and $T_{e_{\alpha}^{\perp},e_{\alpha}^{\perp}}$ are orthogonal projections with sum $I$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] clause (c), [[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]] clause (a)).

[F2] **Outcome law and update.** For a declared ideal sharp measurement with projections $P_{a}$ the probability of the outcome $a$ in a pure state $[\psi]$ is $\|P_{a}\psi\|^{2}$, and after a positive-probability outcome the conditional state is the pure state of $P_{a}\psi$ normalized ([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]] clauses (a)-(b), [[pthm-nrqm-measurement-projective-outcomes-and-discarded-ensembles]] clauses (a)-(b)).

[F3] **Rank-one pairing.** $\operatorname{tr}(T_{x,x}T_{u,u})=|\langle x,u\rangle|^{2}$ for unit vectors $x,u$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] clauses (b)-(c)).

[F4] **Overlaps.** $\langle e_{\alpha},e_{\beta}\rangle=\cos\alpha\cos\beta+\sin\alpha\sin\beta=\cos(\alpha-\beta)$ and $\|e_{\alpha}\|=1$ ([[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]], [[cor-inner-product-induces-a-norm]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct; compute the transition probabilities and conditional states of the declared analyser chain.

1.1 [Clause (i)] The projections of $A(\alpha)$ are the rank-one projections onto the orthonormal pair $(e_{\alpha},e_{\alpha}^{\perp})$ [F1]. By [F2] and [F3], the transmit probability in the preparation $[e_{\beta}]$ is $\|T_{e_{\alpha},e_{\alpha}}e_{\beta}\|^{2}=|\langle e_{\beta},e_{\alpha}\rangle|^{2}=\cos^{2}(\alpha-\beta)$ by [F4], and the conditional state after transmission is the pure state of $T_{e_{\alpha},e_{\alpha}}e_{\beta}=\langle e_{\beta},e_{\alpha}\rangle e_{\alpha}$, which is the pure state of $e_{\alpha}$. This is (i). [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

2.1 [Clause (ii)] Applying step 1.1 successively: the first analyser transmits with probability $\cos^{2}0=1$ and prepares $[e_{x}]$; the second transmits $[e_{x}]$ with probability $\cos^{2}(\pi/4-0)=\tfrac12$ and prepares $[e_{\pi/4}]$; the third transmits $[e_{\pi/4}]$ with probability $\cos^{2}(\pi/2-\pi/4)=\tfrac12$ and prepares $[e_{\pi/2}]$. Multiplying the conditional probabilities by the definition of the sequential update gives the joint transmission probability $\tfrac14$ for the chain. Without the middle analyser the preparation at the third analyser is still $[e_{x}]$, and the transmission probability is $\cos^{2}(\pi/2-0)=0$. This is (ii). [step 1.1, given, F2, F4, algebra]

3.1 [Clauses (iii) and (iv)] Step 2.1 exhibits two declared chains whose transmission probabilities differ even though the first and last analysers are the same, so within the declared model the intervening measurement changes later statistics; this is (iii). For (iv), define the stipulated classical model by the assignment $\text{intensity ratio}(\beta\to\alpha)=|\langle e_{\alpha},e_{\beta}\rangle_{\mathbb R^{2}}|^{2}$ for a unit transverse field along $e_{\beta}$; the same overlap computation [F4] gives $\cos^{2}(\alpha-\beta)$, so the two models agree in this ratio. Since both computations use the same stipulated analyser convention and the same two-dimensional overlap, the agreement is a property of that convention and establishes neither model's applicability to nature nor field quantization; no data are compared. This is (iv). [step 2.1, given, F4, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **Idealisation.** Each analyser is represented by the declared ideal sharp measurement of clause (c) of [[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]: the blocked component is not available for later experiments and the transmitted component leaves the analyser in the corresponding pure state. A physical Polaroid or polarizing beam splitter has its own absorption, reflection, efficiency and background behaviour, which this example does not model.
- **No radiation model.** The two-level space rather than a quantized radiation mode is the declared model; no photon number, mode function, field quantization or Maxwell dynamics is asserted, and no position or arrival-time information is described.
- **Sampling.** The numbers $1,\tfrac12,\tfrac14$ are single-trial model probabilities. A finite run of identically prepared trials would show frequencies that fluctuate about them under any declared sampling model; no such data are reported here.

items.title: An absorbing two-outcome instrument: amplitude suppression and a branch without an outgoing polarization state
items.statement:
Declare a three-level system with assigned Hilbert space $H=\mathbb C^{3}$ and orthonormal basis $(e_{0},e_{1},e_{2})$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-inner-product-space]], [[def-hilbert-space]]). The level $e_{0}$ is a declared **absorbed/no-photon marker** and the plane $\operatorname{span}(e_{1},e_{2})$ is a declared **polarization plane**; this is a finite idealisation of a fixed-mode absorbing detector model, not a radiation model. Fix a unit vector
$$v=\cos\gamma\,e_{1}+\sin\gamma\,e_{2},\qquad v^{\perp}:=-\sin\gamma\,e_{1}+\cos\gamma\,e_{2},$$
so that $(e_{0},v,v^{\perp})$ is an orthonormal basis, and fix a detection parameter $p\in(0,1)$, a dimensionless model parameter. Declare the two-outcome instrument with Kraus family ([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]] clause (d))
$$M_{\mathrm{det}}:=\sqrt p\,T_{e_{0},v},\qquad M_{\mathrm{no}}:=T_{e_{0},e_{0}}+\sqrt{1-p}\,T_{v,v}+T_{v^{\perp},v^{\perp}},$$
where $T_{x,y}z=\langle z,y\rangle x$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]), with outcomes $\mathrm{det}$ and $\mathrm{no}$, effects $F_{\mathrm{det}}=M_{\mathrm{det}}^{*}M_{\mathrm{det}}$, $F_{\mathrm{no}}=M_{\mathrm{no}}^{*}M_{\mathrm{no}}$, probabilities $p_{\mathrm{det}}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{\mathrm{det}})$, $p_{\mathrm{no}}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{\mathrm{no}})$ and updates $\rho\mapsto M_{a}\rho M_{a}^{*}/p_{a}$ for positive probabilities. The example considers preparations $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ with
$$\psi=\alpha v+\beta v^{\perp},\qquad |\alpha|^{2}+|\beta|^{2}=1,$$
so that the preparation lies in the polarization plane, and computes:

**(i)** The family is normalized, $M_{\mathrm{det}}^{*}M_{\mathrm{det}}+M_{\mathrm{no}}^{*}M_{\mathrm{no}}=I$, with effects $F_{\mathrm{det}}=p\,T_{v,v}$ and $F_{\mathrm{no}}=T_{e_{0},e_{0}}+(1-p)T_{v,v}+T_{v^{\perp},v^{\perp}}$; hence
$$p_{\mathrm{det}}=p\,|\alpha|^{2},\qquad p_{\mathrm{no}}=1-p\,|\alpha|^{2}.$$

**(ii)** Conditioned on the outcome $\mathrm{det}$, the conditional state is $T_{e_{0},e_{0}}$: the branch carries the absorbed/no-photon record and leaves **no outgoing state in the polarization plane**. In particular the model does not produce an outgoing one-photon polarization state for the detected branch.

**(iii)** Conditioned on the outcome $\mathrm{no}$, the conditional state is the pure state of the normalized vector
$$\frac{\sqrt{1-p}\,\alpha\,v+\beta\,v^{\perp}}{\sqrt{(1-p)|\alpha|^{2}+|\beta|^{2}}},$$
that is, the $v$-component is amplitude-suppressed by $\sqrt{1-p}$ rather than projected away. For the fully detectable preparation $\psi=v$ ($\alpha=1$) and $p=\tfrac12$ one has $p_{\mathrm{det}}=p_{\mathrm{no}}=\tfrac12$ and the no-detection conditional state is again $T_{v,v}$; a repetition of the instrument on that branch again detects with probability $\tfrac12$, so the no-detection outcome is not repeatable.

**(iv)** After the detection branch the state is $T_{e_{0},e_{0}}$, and a repetition gives $p_{\mathrm{det}}=\operatorname{tr}(T_{e_{0},e_{0}}F_{\mathrm{det}})=p|\langle e_{0},v\rangle|^{2}=0$: the detection outcome is not repeatable either. The effects $F_{\mathrm{det}}$ and $F_{\mathrm{no}}$ are not projections for $0<p<1$, so the instrument is not a declared ideal sharp measurement; it is a declared general instrument whose update is part of its declaration ([[pthm-nrqm-measurement-instrument-updates-not-determined-by-effects]], clause (v) of the ideal conditional-measurement postulate).

No real detector, efficiency, dark count, dead time, photon number or measured rate is described; the computation is a model computation in the declared three-level space.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The three-level Hilbert space $H=\mathbb C^{3}$ with orthonormal basis $(e_{0},e_{1},e_{2})$; the unit vector $v$ and $v^{\perp}$; the parameter $p\in(0,1)$; the Kraus family $M_{\mathrm{det}},M_{\mathrm{no}}$ and its outcomes; a pure preparation of $\psi=\alpha v+\beta v^{\perp}$ with $|\alpha|^{2}+|\beta|^{2}=1$.

[F1] **Rank-one calculus in $\mathbb C^{3}$.** $T_{x,y}z=\langle z,y\rangle x$ satisfies $T_{x,y}^{*}=T_{y,x}$, $T_{x,y}T_{u,w}=\langle u,y\rangle T_{x,w}$, and for an orthonormal basis $(b_{1},b_{2},b_{3})$ one has $\sum_{i}T_{b_{i},b_{i}}=I$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] clauses (a)-(d), [[def-hilbert-space]]).

[F2] **Declared instruments.** A normalized finite Kraus family $(M_{a})$ with $\sum_{a}M_{a}^{*}M_{a}=I$ declares an instrument with effects $F_{a}=M_{a}^{*}M_{a}$, outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$ and conditional updates $M_{a}\rho M_{a}^{*}/p_{a}$ for $p_{a}>0$ ([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]] clause (d), [[pthm-nrqm-measurement-countable-kraus-instruments]] clauses (a)-(b), [[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]] clauses (a)-(b)).

[F3] **States.** $T_{\psi,\psi}$ with $\|\psi\|=1$ is a state, and for a rank-one weight $T_{x,x}$ with $\|x\|=1$ one has $\operatorname{tr}(T_{x,x}S)=\langle Sx,x\rangle$ for bounded $S$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a), [F1]).

[F4] **Elementary inner products.** $\langle v,v\rangle=\langle v^{\perp},v^{\perp}\rangle=1$, $\langle v,v^{\perp}\rangle=0$, and $\langle e_{0},v\rangle=0$ ([[cor-inner-product-induces-a-norm]], [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct; verify normalization of the declared Kraus family and compute the two branches on the explicit three-dimensional data.

1.1 [Normalization and effects] By [F1], $M_{\mathrm{det}}^{*}M_{\mathrm{det}}=p\,T_{v,v}$ and $M_{\mathrm{no}}^{*}M_{\mathrm{no}}=T_{e_{0},e_{0}}+(1-p)T_{v,v}+T_{v^{\perp},v^{\perp}}$, since the cross terms of $M_{\mathrm{no}}$ vanish by the orthogonality relations $\langle e_{0},v\rangle=\langle v,v^{\perp}\rangle=0$ [F4]; summing gives $p\,T_{v,v}+T_{e_{0},e_{0}}+(1-p)T_{v,v}+T_{v^{\perp},v^{\perp}}=T_{e_{0},e_{0}}+T_{v,v}+T_{v^{\perp},v^{\perp}}=I$ by [F1]. Hence the family is normalized with the displayed effects [F2]. [given, F1, F2, F4, algebra]

2.1 [Clause (i)] By [F2] and [F3], $p_{\mathrm{det}}=\operatorname{tr}(T_{\psi,\psi}F_{\mathrm{det}})=\langle F_{\mathrm{det}}\psi,\psi\rangle=p|\langle\psi,v\rangle|^{2}=p|\alpha|^{2}$ and $p_{\mathrm{no}}=1-p_{\mathrm{det}}=1-p|\alpha|^{2}$, using $\langle\psi,v\rangle=\alpha$ [F4]. This is (i). [step 1.1, given, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

3.1 [Clause (ii): the absorbed branch] The non-normalized conditional operator is $M_{\mathrm{det}}\rho M_{\mathrm{det}}^{*}=pT_{e_{0},v}T_{\psi,\psi}T_{v,e_{0}}=p|\langle\psi,v\rangle|^{2}T_{e_{0},e_{0}}=p_{\mathrm{det}}T_{e_{0},e_{0}}$ by [F1]; dividing by $p_{\mathrm{det}}>0$ (for $\alpha\ne0$) gives $T_{e_{0},e_{0}}$, a state with no component in the polarization plane. This is (ii). [step 2.1, given, F1, F3, algebra]

3.2 [Clause (iii): the non-detection branch] Since $M_{\mathrm{no}}\psi=\sqrt{1-p}\alpha v+\beta v^{\perp}$ by [F1] and [F4], the non-normalized conditional operator is $T_{M_{\mathrm{no}}\psi,M_{\mathrm{no}}\psi}$ with trace $\|M_{\mathrm{no}}\psi\|^{2}=(1-p)|\alpha|^{2}+|\beta|^{2}=p_{\mathrm{no}}$; dividing gives the pure state of the displayed normalized vector, in which the $v$-amplitude is scaled by $\sqrt{1-p}$ instead of being removed. For $\alpha=1$, $\beta=0$ and $p=\tfrac12$ the vector is $v$ and the state is again $T_{v,v}$; applying the formulas of (i) to this state gives $p_{\mathrm{det}}=\tfrac12$ once more, so the no-detection outcome does not repeat with certainty. This is (iii). [step 2.1, given, F1, F3, F4, algebra]

4.1 [Clause (iv): the detected branch and the idealisation] On the state $T_{e_{0},e_{0}}$ of step 3.1 the detection probability is $\operatorname{tr}(T_{e_{0},e_{0}}F_{\mathrm{det}})=p|\langle e_{0},v\rangle|^{2}=0$ by [F3] and [F4], so the detection outcome does not repeat either; and $F_{\mathrm{det}}=pT_{v,v}$ has the eigenvalues $p,0,0$, so it is not a projection when $0<p<1$, and the instrument is not a declared ideal sharp measurement. The update of the non-detection branch is therefore not the Lueders update of a projection, and its value is part of the declaration [F2], in agreement with the non-determination recorded in [[pthm-nrqm-measurement-instrument-updates-not-determined-by-effects]]. No detector quantity was used. This is (iv). [step 3.2, given, F1, F2, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **Interpretation of the marker.** The level $e_{0}$ is a bookkeeping record of the branch in which the model detector has absorbed the excitation of the polarization mode. The example is honest about being a declared three-level idealisation: it asserts no photon-number content, no outgoing vacuum field, no detector dynamics and no real absorption mechanism.
- **Why this is not a projection.** The effects $F_{\mathrm{det}}$ and $F_{\mathrm{no}}$ sum to $I$ and have eigenvalues in $[0,1]$, so they are legitimate effects of a finite-resolution apparatus model; the principal contrast with the projective case is that the update of the no-detection branch suppresses the detected component by the amplitude $\sqrt{1-p}$ rather than projecting it away, and that neither outcome is repeatable.

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 1.3.6, printed pages 14-15 (photons passed or absorbed by an analyser, with the transmitted state fixed by the analyser)

items.title: Coarse and fine declared measurements of a degenerate subspace: the Lueders update is not eigenvector selection
items.statement:
Declare a three-level system with assigned Hilbert space $H=\mathbb C^{3}$ and orthonormal basis $(e_{1},e_{2},e_{3})$, and put
$$K:=\operatorname{span}(e_{1},e_{2}),\qquad P:=T_{e_{1},e_{1}}+T_{e_{2},e_{2}},\qquad \psi:=\frac{e_{1}+e_{2}}{\sqrt2},\qquad w':=\frac{e_{1}-e_{2}}{\sqrt2},$$
with $T_{x,y}z=\langle z,y\rangle x$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-inner-product-space]], [[def-hilbert-space]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]). Declare the two ideal sharp measurements
$$\mathcal C:=(P,\,I-P)\quad\text{(coarse readout of }K\text{)},\qquad \mathcal G:=(T_{e_{1},e_{1}},\,T_{e_{2},e_{2}},\,T_{e_{3},e_{3}})\quad\text{(fine readout)},$$
and consider the pure preparation $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ and the bounded self-adjoint observable
$$W:=T_{\psi,\psi}-T_{w',w'}$$
with spectral projections $T_{\psi,\psi}$ at $+1$, $T_{w',w'}$ at $-1$ and $I-T_{\psi,\psi}-T_{w',w'}$ at $0$ ([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]], [[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]). Then:

**(i)** In the coarse measurement $\mathcal C$ the outcome $K$ has probability $1$, and the conditional state is again $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$: the coarse readout leaves the coherent superposition inside the degenerate subspace intact.

**(ii)** In the fine measurement $\mathcal G$ the outcomes $e_{1}$ and $e_{2}$ have probabilities $\tfrac12$ each (and $e_{3}$ has probability $0$), with conditional states $T_{e_{1},e_{1}}$ and $T_{e_{2},e_{2}}$: the fine readout selects a basis state.

**(iii)** For the observable $W$ the two declared measurements give different model predictions: after the coarse outcome the value $+1$ has probability $1$; the mixture $\tfrac12T_{e_{1},e_{1}}+\tfrac12T_{e_{2},e_{2}}$ (the discarded ensemble of the fine measurement) assigns probability $\tfrac12$ to $+1$ and $\tfrac12$ to $-1$. Hence the coarse Lueders update is not equivalent to selecting one eigenvector of the degenerate subspace with probability $\tfrac12$ and forgetting the other: that replacement destroys the coherence of $\psi$ and changes the statistics of $W$.

**(iv)** The fine measurement is a different declared measurement, not a refinement of the reported data of the coarse one. A model that reports only "the system is in $K$" and then predicts with the mixture of (iii) is a different model from the coarse Lueders model, with the observable consequence exhibited in (iii). No apparatus is asserted to realize either declared measurement, and no empirical comparison is made.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The three-level Hilbert space $H=\mathbb C^{3}$ with orthonormal basis $(e_{1},e_{2},e_{3})$; the projection $P=T_{e_{1},e_{1}}+T_{e_{2},e_{2}}$; the unit vectors $\psi,w'$; the declared measurements $\mathcal C,\mathcal G$; the preparation $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$; the observable $W$.

[F1] **Rank-one calculus.** $T_{x,y}z=\langle z,y\rangle x$ is trace class with $T_{x,y}^{*}=T_{y,x}$; for unit vectors $x,u$ the operator $T_{x,x}$ is an orthogonal projection with $\operatorname{tr}(T_{x,x}S)=\langle Sx,x\rangle$ for bounded $S$, and $\operatorname{tr}(T_{x,x}T_{u,u})=|\langle x,u\rangle|^{2}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] clauses (b)-(d), [[def-hilbert-space]]).

[F2] **Declared measurements and updates.** For a declared ideal sharp measurement $(P_{a})$ the outcome probabilities are $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})=\|P_{a}\xi\|^{2}$ for a pure preparation of the unit vector $\xi$, and the conditional state after a positive-probability outcome is $P_{a}\rho P_{a}/p_{a}$ ([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]] clauses (a)-(b), [[pthm-nrqm-measurement-projective-outcomes-and-discarded-ensembles]] clauses (a)-(b)).

[F3] **Coherence in a degenerate eigenspace.** If $\xi$ lies in the range of a projection $P$ and $\rho=T_{\xi,\xi}$, the conditional state after the outcome of the two-outcome measurement $(P,I-P)$ is again $T_{\xi,\xi}$ ([[pthm-nrqm-measurement-degenerate-eigenspace-update]] clause (a)).

[F4] **Spectral projections of $W$.** $\psi$ and $w'$ are orthonormal, and $W=T_{\psi,\psi}-T_{w',w'}$ is bounded and self-adjoint with $W\psi=\psi$, $Ww'=-w'$, so $T_{\psi,\psi}$ and $T_{w',w'}$ are its spectral projections at $+1$ and $-1$ ([[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]], [F1]).

[F5] **Elementary overlaps.** $\langle e_{1},\psi\rangle=\langle e_{2},\psi\rangle=1/\sqrt2$, $\langle e_{1},w'\rangle=1/\sqrt2$, $\langle e_{2},w'\rangle=-1/\sqrt2$, and $\langle e_{3},\psi\rangle=\langle e_{3},w'\rangle=0$ ([[cor-inner-product-induces-a-norm]], [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]]).

## Verification

**Proof technique:** direct; compute the outcome laws and conditional states of the two declared measurements and the induced law of the observable $W$.

1.1 [Clause (i)] $P\psi=\psi$, so [F2] gives $\operatorname{tr}(\rho P)=\|P\psi\|^{2}=1$; by [F3] the conditional state after the outcome $K$ is $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$, unchanged. This is (i). [given, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 [Clause (ii)] By [F2] and [F1], the fine outcome probabilities are $\operatorname{tr}(T_{\psi,\psi}T_{e_{i},e_{i}})=|\langle e_{i},\psi\rangle|^{2}$, equal to $\tfrac12$ for $i=1,2$ and $0$ for $i=3$ by [F5]; the conditional states are $T_{e_{i},e_{i}}$. This is (ii). [step 1.1, given, F1, F2, F5, algebra]

3.1 [Clause (iii)] By [F4] and [F2], in the coarse conditional state $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ the value $+1$ of $W$ has probability $\operatorname{tr}(T_{\psi,\psi}T_{\psi,\psi})=1$. The mixture $\sigma=\tfrac12T_{e_{1},e_{1}}+\tfrac12T_{e_{2},e_{2}}$ gives $\operatorname{tr}(\sigma T_{\psi,\psi})=\tfrac12|\langle e_{1},\psi\rangle|^{2}+\tfrac12|\langle e_{2},\psi\rangle|^{2}=\tfrac12$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\sigma T_{w',w'})=\tfrac12|\langle e_{1},w'\rangle|^{2}+\tfrac12|\langle e_{2},w'\rangle|^{2}=\tfrac12$ by [F1] and [F5], so the mixture assigns probability $\tfrac12$ to each of $+1$ and $-1$. The two laws for $W$ differ; the discarded ensemble of the fine measurement is this mixture, whereas the coarse conditional state is the coherent state $\rho$, so replacing the coarse Lueders update by eigenvector selection is a distinct model with different predictions. This is (iii). [step 2.1, given, F1, F2, F4, F5, algebra]

4.1 [Clause (iv) and scope] The measurements $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal G$ have different outcome structures ($\mathcal G$ resolves $K$, $\mathcal C$ does not), so $\mathcal G$ is not a re-reading of coarse data; and step 3.1 shows that the coarse Lueders model and the eigenvector-selection mixture differ in the law of the declared observable $W$. No apparatus was used and no record is reported. This is (iv). [step 3.1, given, F2, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **Degeneracy is a property of the declared measurement, not of the state alone.** The superposition $\psi$ inside $K$ is unchanged by the coarse readout because the update uses the projection onto the whole eigenspace; a fine measurement whose projections lie inside $K$ is a different apparatus model with different outcomes.
- **No preferred basis.** The coarse readout has no rule that selects $e_{1}$ or $e_{2}$; the model contains no such rule, and the example shows that adding one changes predictions for a suitable later observable.

The example shows that the Lueders update by the subspace projection retains the coherent superposition while the fine measurement selects basis states, and that the two declared measurements give different statistics for a suitable bounded observable. It asserts no apparatus realization and no empirical result.

items.title: What the worked instruments of the companion page establish
items.statement:
**Serial filters.** [[ex-nrqm-measurement-serial-stern-gerlach-filters]] computes, in a declared two-level spin-half model with the spin assignment of P6, the outcome probabilities $\cos^{2}(\theta/2)$ and $\cos^{2}((\varphi-\theta)/2)$ of successive ideal filters and the quarter-probability case. The computation verifies the model's serial Lueders statistics for declared ideal filters. It does not derive the inhomogeneous-field force, the spatial splitting or the detector response of a Stern-Gerlach apparatus, and it reports no measured fraction and no property of silver atoms; the reported Stern-Gerlach experiments of 1922 remain a candidate experiment item that is not asserted by this page.

**Analyser chain.** [[ex-nrqm-measurement-three-polarizer-chain]] computes the transmission probabilities of a chain of declared ideal analysers in a declared two-level model and exhibits the standard $\tfrac14$ case, together with an explicit caveat that a stipulated classical amplitude model with the same ideal analyser convention gives the same ratio. The agreement of the two model computations does not establish field quantization or the applicability of either model to nature, and no transmission counts, efficiencies or backgrounds are reported.

**Absorbing instrument.** [[ex-nrqm-measurement-absorption-instrument]] exhibits a declared two-outcome instrument whose detected branch leaves an absorbed marker with no outgoing polarization-plane state and whose non-detection branch suppresses one amplitude by $\sqrt{1-p}$ rather than projecting it away; neither outcome is repeatable. The computation verifies that a declared instrument can describe a destructive apparatus within the framework's instrument vocabulary and that its update is part of its declaration. The three-level space is an idealisation; no real detector, photon number, efficiency or rate is described.

**Degenerate readout versus fine readout.** [[ex-nrqm-measurement-degenerate-coarse-versus-fine-update]] contrasts a coarse readout of a degenerate subspace with a fine readout resolving it and shows that the coarse Lueders update retains the coherent superposition while the eigenvector-selection mixture changes the law of a suitable bounded observable. The computation verifies the degeneracy clause of the projective update inside an explicit three-level model; it asserts no preferred basis and no apparatus.

**Empirical neutrality.** None of the four items is an experiment. Each is a finite computation for a declared preparation and a declared measurement model; none records data, calibration, sampling, uncertainty or a comparison with observation, and none claims that a laboratory device realizes the declared instrument. Agreement or disagreement with data would test the combined model and apparatus assumptions under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]) and is not established or claimed here.
